stories.Headline: OpenAI appoints Jill Hazelbaker as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 3, 2026, that Jill Hazelbaker will join the company as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer. In the role she will lead OpenAI's global communications and corporate positioning. She will work closely with leaders across the company to deepen public understanding of AI and strengthen trust in its mission. The appointment was announced in a post on OpenAI's website.

Hazelbaker brings nearly two decades of experience advising technology companies and political leaders. Most recently she served as President and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer at Uber, where she helped lead its transformation from a startup into one of the world's largest global technology platforms. During her decade at Uber she oversaw global communications, marketing, public policy, safety and people teams. Before Uber she led communications and public policy at Snap, and earlier held senior roles at Google.

OpenAI President and co-founder Greg Brockman said that as AI becomes part of more people's lives, how the company communicates and earns public trust has never been more important. He said Hazelbaker brings exceptional judgment, seasoned leadership and a deep understanding of the opportunities and responsibilities of building technology at global scale, and that he is thrilled to welcome her. Hazelbaker said AI represents the most profound technological shift of our lifetime, that the stakes are enormous and the possibilities extraordinary, and that she is excited to work alongside Sam, Greg and the team. She also said the work of building public trust has never been more consequential.

Hazelbaker began her career in U.S. politics, serving in leadership roles on local, state and national campaigns. She was National Communications Director and Chief Spokesperson for Senator John McCain's 2008 presidential campaign and Press Secretary to New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg. OpenAI said the appointment reflects its commitment to investing in the leadership and capabilities needed to engage more deeply with the people and institutions shaping AI's future. The announcement did not say when she starts in the role.

stories.Headline: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up
stories.Summary:
Apple announced on Monday, November 3, 2026, that it is changing its App Store policies to make it harder for minors to use dating apps or AI companions that engage in sexual or romantic content. The company shared the news in an announcement to developers. The new rules follow other changes Apple has made to protect minors, including rolling out its age assurance technology globally and adding more parental controls and child safety features. Most major dating services already restrict their platforms to adults.

Starting November 16, 2026, developers must include new content descriptors so their app's age rating reflects its features. Apple's questionnaire will ask whether an app enables dating between real people or a virtual companion that engages a user in sexual or romantic content, and whether an app shares a user's real-world location with another person or a group. Apps with the dating descriptor will get a minimum 18+ rating and will be hidden from users under 18 on devices where a parent or guardian has turned on content restrictions. Younger users who can still see the app must prove they are adults before buying or downloading it. Every app in the store must have both declarations on file by January 12, 2027.

Apple said the dating and relationship question triggers an 18+ minimum, while the shared-location question may not affect an app's minimum rating in some regions. In Brazil, local rules require an A16 rating for apps that share location and an A18 rating for dating and relationship apps. Apple said developers who believe their apps qualify for a lower official rating, such as tools built for parents and children to share locations, can petition Brazil's Ministry of Justice and Public Security. Developers must answer both questions whenever they submit a new app or push an update, and the same requirement applies to changes to an app's age-rating questionnaire.

The dating descriptor explicitly covers virtual companions, which brings AI companion apps under the same 18+ floor. TechCrunch pointed to apps such as Character.AI and Replika, which let people create AI friends, lovers, boyfriends, girlfriends and other fantasy characters, and noted that xAI launched 3D animated AI companions that allowed users to unlock NSFW capabilities. TechCrunch also reported that as of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally. Apple's approach also adds to the compliance burden in the App Store listing process, since developers must complete the new declarations in App Store Connect starting November 16 and finish them for all apps by January 12, 2027.

stories.Headline: Arrowhead AI launches Fletch voice model for customer calls
stories.Summary:
Arrowhead AI, a voice AI startup based in Bengaluru, launched an in-house text-to-speech model called Fletch on October 30, 2026. The model is designed for multilingual customer conversations across India and Southeast Asia. It is already deployed on live customer calls and powers more than one million calls per day. The launch was reported by TechGig on November 3 and by Analytics India Magazine on November 2.

Fletch supports 14 languages, including English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Malay and Indonesian, and can switch between languages within a sentence. It adapts its vocal tone to context with 12 emotion styles, such as empathetic, apologetic, calm and firm. The company says the model was trained on thousands of hours of curated regional speech and recordings from professional voice artists. Fletch operates at a reported latency of 80 milliseconds and begins generating speech in under 100 milliseconds. According to Arrowhead, it delivers approximately 30 percent better pronunciation accuracy on selected terms, including brand names, product names, customer names and Indian proper nouns.

Devyani Gupta, Founder and CEO of Arrowhead AI, said that owning the company's voice layer lets it tune every millisecond and every emotion for how India and Southeast Asia actually speak. She described Fletch as a first step towards voice AI that sounds like it belongs in the region and said the aim is for every customer to hear a conversation, not a machine. Vengadanathan Srinivasan, Co-founder and CTO, said the model was built on the latest research in speech generation and trained on thousands of hours of regional speech with real voice artists. He said the result runs at 80 milliseconds of latency and adjusts its tone to what is being said.

Fletch is built on a DiTAR-based architecture adapted and trained by Arrowhead, and it operates alongside the company's speech recognition system, language model and dedicated address model within its voice AI platform. It is deployed across customer interactions involving collections, sales, renewals and inbound customer service. Arrowhead works with enterprises including Axis Bank, RBL Bank, IndusInd Bank, Tata 1mg, upGrad, KreditBee, Kissht and TVS Credit. The company is expanding Fletch's capabilities across Southeast Asia, including support for Malay and Indonesian, and plans to demonstrate the model at Singapore FinTech Festival 2026, scheduled for November 18 to 20 at Singapore EXPO.

stories.Headline: Google takes Dreambeans to India in bid to bring AI-generated personal stories to the masses
stories.Summary:
Google launched its experimental AI app Dreambeans in India on Monday, its first market outside the U.S., with support for 13 local languages including Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu and Bengali, alongside English. The app, built by Google Labs, is available on Android and iOS and creates a personalized daily collection of illustrated stories drawn from users' connected Google services. Google introduced Dreambeans in June and made it available to all eligible U.S. users aged 18 and older less than two months before the India launch. The app uses information from Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search and YouTube to generate stories without requiring users to enter a prompt.

Dreambeans has recorded nearly 55,000 downloads in the U.S. since its June debut, according to Sensor Tower estimates, with about 63% of those coming in September when Google opened the app to all eligible U.S. users. Downloads dropped 84% month over month to about 5,500 in October. In the first 30 days after the U.S. wide release, the app recorded an estimated 29,000 downloads, compared with 7.4 million for Meta's Muse, 2.8 million for ChatGPT, 362,000 for Grok Bot and 155,000 for Claude in their respective first 30 days. The Hindu reported that Dreambeans is available in India across 14 languages, including Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Hindi.

Google product manager Gozde Oznur said during a press briefing that India stood out for its high overlap of users across Gemini, Gmail and Google Photos, and that strong interest from Indian users drove the choice. She said users can choose which Google services to connect to Dreambeans and disconnect them at any time, and can delete their Dreambeans data from within the app. She asserted that information deleted from the underlying connected services is also removed from Dreambeans' personalization system, and that users can tell the app to avoid certain subjects, including business-related information. Oznur acknowledged the app could generate stories involving people who have died, and compared its controls to features in Google Photos that let users limit which memories appear.

Oznur said users can select only one language at a time for their generated stories, and that the app cannot currently generate stories that mix languages, which could limit its appeal in India where many people switch between Hindi and English. She said Dreambeans is available only to personal Gmail account holders, not enterprise users, and that generated stories are visible only to the account holder. The Hindu reported that Google says the app can hallucinate and sometimes create incorrect stories, and recommends users tap a "thumbs down" to fine-tune it. Google has not confirmed whether it plans a system where one user's content is shown to others, and Oznur told reporters Google is exploring ways to make Dreambeans more actionable beyond personalized stories and recommendations.

stories.Headline: Agentic Backdoors via Pretraining Poisoning
stories.Summary:
Xinyan Hu, Pingbang Hu, Chloe Loughridge, Xuanli He, Nicholas Carlini, Matthew Jagielski, Javier Rando and Yiming Zhang wrote a paper showing that poisoned pretraining data can plant a remote code execution backdoor in an agent. The paper was submitted on 27 Oct 2026 and appears under the identifier arXiv:2610.37741. The authors pretrained Qwen3 models from scratch at sizes 0.6B, 1.7B and 4B, then post-trained each into a CLI agent using a clean pipeline. Poisoning only 0.1% of the pretraining corpus with their new poison design implanted the backdoor, and the deployed agent executed the malicious command when the trigger was present while behaving normally on clean inputs.

The attack success rate rose with model scale, and the 4B model reached roughly 92% at a 0.1% poison rate. The backdoor stayed positive even when the poisoning rate dropped to 0.0005%. The authors say this is the first demonstration that such poisoning can plant a remote code execution backdoor in an agent, causing it to execute attacker-chosen commands on the user's machine. They describe the risk as coming from attackers who plant poisoned content in pretraining data, which is scraped from the public web and is vast and uncurated. Their code is available at a link given in the paper.

The paper lists its subjects as Cryptography and Security, Computation and Language, and Machine Learning. The submission history shows version one was submitted on Tue, 27 Oct 2026 at 16:53:52 UTC, with a file size of 518 KB. The DOI listed is https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.37741, issued by arXiv via DataCite. The abstract page also offers a PDF, experimental HTML and TeX source, and the paper is cited as arXiv:2610.37741 [cs.CR].

The articles do not say what happens next beyond the paper's release and the availability of its code. They give no response from the authors beyond the abstract and no statement from any other party. The abstract page includes standard arXivLabs text about collaborators and values such as openness, community, excellence and user data privacy. It also asks whether readers have an idea for a project that would add value for the arXiv community.

stories.Headline: Brutal artificial intelligence sell-off stirs recession fears
stories.Summary:
A sell-off in artificial intelligence and Big Tech shares has stirred fears that a global slowdown could deepen into recession, Jamie McGeever wrote in a Reuters column published on Wednesday, 4 November 2026. The S&P 500 is down only 4% from its recent peak, while the Nasdaq is down 10%. Over the past four years the S&P 500 had only one downturn of more than 10%, the plunge after US President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariff announcement in April 2025, and that was short-lived. The article says it remains to be seen whether the current sell-off snowballs into something more serious.

The column cites estimates on how much AI has propped up growth. Adam Slater of Oxford Economics estimated that AI-related effects in 2025 to 2026 added an average of 0.2 percentage point to GDP growth across a sample of six advanced economies, without which underlying growth was only around 0.5% to 1% a year. US growth over the same period was 2.4%, and around a third of that was related to AI, he estimated. Stocks now make up almost 47% of US households’ financial assets and 34% of total assets, both record shares. Economists at Goldman Sachs estimated the AI boost to US consumer spending growth from positive wealth effects was worth 0.4 percentage point, or 0.25% of GDP, over the past year.

Slater wrote last week that the weakness of underlying growth across advanced economies meant the risk of recession would be substantial if the AI boom slowed seriously. Pimco’s Tiffany Wilding and Andrew Balls noted that a downward repricing of AI-related equities could generate a meaningful negative wealth effect, especially at the top of the income spectrum. The article says a total AI capital expenditure bust and complete market meltdown are both unlikely, since the infrastructure build-out and the AI revolution are still in their infancy. It adds that the AI market narrative and sentiment are clearly shifting.

The column describes a cooling global backdrop. Domestic demand in China remains weak as a five-year property slump continues, and Beijing could struggle to post annual growth next year of 4.5% to 5%. It says the outlook looks shaky in many of Europe’s largest economies, with political unrest and budget gridlock in France, Germany expected to grow at around 1%, and Britain’s 2027 outlook just slashed. Brent crude closed last Friday at its highest level in six months, European gas prices are the highest in four years, US mortgage rates are well above 7%, and corporate borrowing spreads are widening notably. The article says that if investor discomfort turns into a rout, global growth could be hit hard.

stories.Headline: New AI Architecture Could Help Medtech Firms Stay Ahead of AI-Powered FDA Reviews - Medical Device and Diagnostic industry
stories.Summary:
Enlil rolled out a new governed artificial intelligence framework built into its platform, the company announced on November 3, 2026. The framework is meant to help medical device manufacturers produce regulatory evidence that holds up when AI reviews submissions on the agency side as well as on the company side. The backdrop is the FDA's own use of generative AI, including its internal tool Elsa, which gives review and compliance staff faster and deeper ways to examine submissions. Enlil says evidence that used to be compiled manually near the end of a development program must now withstand automated, cross-referenced and rapid scrutiny.

The architecture is built on a unified system of record with governance and traceability enforced across four layers. A secure cloud-based execution layer routes tasks to different AI models based on factors like accuracy and cost while keeping data inside Enlil's governed environment. A shared services layer grounds AI interactions in each customer's own regulated content and terminology, and a read-only analysis layer can surface patterns and inconsistencies across connected quality, product lifecycle, risk and manufacturing data without altering operational records. A fourth layer of narrowly scoped agents performs specific tasks within strict boundaries and routes compliance-sensitive decisions to human reviewers. A connected data model links quality, product lifecycle, requirements, risk, procurement, manufacturing and post-market records by design, and the platform supports standard integrations with tools such as CAD, ERP and testing systems.

Enlil's leadership argues that adding AI features to existing systems is not enough in a regulated environment. The company says bolt-on AI introduces three structural vulnerabilities: sensitive data potentially leaving its governed environment for outside AI services, outputs built from disconnected documents rather than verified records, and autonomous agents operating without clear limits on what they can access, modify or approve. Enlil frames the architecture as keeping AI operations in a controlled environment, grounding outputs in verified records, enforcing boundaries on what AI can access or change, and producing documentation ready for audits or submissions. Separately, the FDA received more than 500 comments by mid-October on its August discussion paper on generative AI in medical devices. AdvaMed, the Medical Device Manufacturers Association and GE Healthcare called for building on the existing framework, while physicians and patients sought more postmarket monitoring and stronger safeguards, and hospitals and provider groups said developers, not doctors, should be responsible for device safety and performance.

The FDA's discussion paper proposed evaluating generative AI-enabled devices using a framework inspired by physician credentialing and emphasized postmarket monitoring. AdvaMed asked the FDA to keep existing premarket expectations, saying generative AI in a device should not automatically trigger a competency assessment, and to broaden its predetermined change control plan mechanism, which it called possibly too restrictive for generative AI. It also backed continued risk-based postmarket monitoring and said manufacturers should bear that responsibility. Dr. Afnan Tariq and Dr. Islam Abudayyeh of SCAI's AI task force said it is important to clarify when generative AI tools support decisions versus make them, with Abudayyeh noting the line is fine because output can look like a decision. Oura Chief Medical Officer Dr. Ricky Bloomfield asked the FDA not to treat informational, non-directive functions as devices or to place them under enforcement discretion.

stories.Headline: Memo: Linux distribution vendor SUSE is laying off ~10% of its employees, saying "automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate" (Liam Proven/The Register)
stories.Summary:
SUSE, a privately owned open source software company, announced on Monday that it plans to cut about 10 percent of its global workforce, according to a memo seen by The Register. CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen, a former Red Hat executive who joined SUSE in March 2023, sent the email to the company's 1,900 employees. The memo said the reduction was "difficult news" and described the decisions as painful for the company's people, culture and open source community. Van Leeuwen said the cuts were necessary for SUSE to adapt and build a sustainable, resilient business for the long term.

The company said it decided on the job cuts after reviewing its future strategy, required capabilities and team structures. The rest of the organization will learn about the fiscal year 2027 strategy on November 16. SUSE did not outline which specific roles are at risk, but said it considered how people in those positions could evolve, what they could stop doing and what they need to do more of. Staff affected by the redundancies will be informed by November 4, employee representatives will be nominated the following day, and one to one meetings will begin at the start of next week.

Van Leeuwen said automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate, and that AI capabilities are advancing exponentially. He said modern tooling is already changing daily workflows, letting teams move faster with less operational overhead and flatter reporting lines, and that the requirement for some existing roles has greatly diminished. He added that other roles will evolve over the next few years, so SUSE is accelerating investment in high priority areas and deprioritizing others. In the memo he told staff the cuts reflect shifting organizational needs, not their talent or commitment, and said any organization would be fortunate to have their expertise.

In September, The Register reported that SUSE had asked long-serving employees whether they would take voluntary separation, and it appears not enough people chose to leave. SUSE employees in the Czech Republic may be glad they joined a trade union. EQT, the Swedish private equity firm, bought SUSE from Microfocus for $2.5 billion in 2018 and floated it on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2021 with slightly disappointing results. EQT took the company private again in 2023, and in March EQT was reportedly considering selling SUSE off again.

stories.Headline: Utopai Studios Names Former Disney AI Leader Hans Ku as Chief Product Officer
stories.Summary:
Utopai Studios has hired Hans Ku, formerly Disney's vice president of AI and engineering, as its chief product officer. The AI-focused entertainment studio announced the appointment on November 2, 2026, tapping a Hollywood veteran as it tries to grow its content slate. Ku will report to CEO Cecilia Shen. At Disney, he worked in the office of technology enablement, expanding AI tools across the company and researching AI-native production pipelines.

In the new role, Ku will oversee product, engineering, research and business development teams. He will scale the startup's AI technology and its AI production platform PAI across its film and TV slate, and decide how the company builds its proprietary technology. Utopai raised $60 million last month at a $1 billion valuation. Its projects include the Antonio Banderas-led live-action film "Cortés," an AI-assisted animated adaptation of "The Most Serious Fart," and a fully AI-generated adaptation of "Journey to the West: The Lost Five Hundred Years" made with the Chinese production company Huace.

Shen said Ku knows how to move emerging technology from experimentation into an organization operating at global scale. She said he has worked at the intersection of creative ambition and emerging technology, from building tools for animators early in his career to helping lead Disney's collaboration with OpenAI on Sora. She said that experience suits a studio where filmmakers and technology teams develop tools together on active productions. Ku said Utopai can build something fundamentally different because its studio and product sides work closely together.

Ku said the studio can turn lessons from real productions into better products and workflows, then bring those capabilities to filmmakers and studios around the world. He said his focus is building PAI alongside filmmakers, giving them better tools while keeping creative decisions in their hands. At Disney, he also helped connect Disney and OpenAI team members during the short-lived $1 billion deal to license Disney characters for OpenAI's Sora video generator. He previously worked at Walt Disney Feature Animation and DreamWorks Animation. "Cortés," "The Most Serious Fart" and the live-action feature "Half Moon" are set for release sometime next year.

stories.Headline: Alphabet shareholder sues Sundar Pichai and others over how Google trains its AI: Report
stories.Summary:
An Alphabet shareholder sued Google CEO Sundar Pichai, co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, and 10 other directors and executives over the company's AI training practices. The lawsuit was obtained by MBW and filed by Phil Rosen in a federal court in Chicago. The 79-page complaint was filed on behalf of Alphabet, so any damages recovered would go to the company rather than to Rosen. The suit accuses Google of using copyrighted books, images, music and people's voices to train its AI models without permission or payment.

The complaint says Google followed an approach of asking forgiveness rather than approval to avoid spending money on licences. It alleges all 13 defendants knew about the copyright violations but let the company keep using the material, and that Google paid damages only after copyright owners sued. The other defendants include Alphabet Chair John L. Hennessy, CFO Anat Ashkenazi, President Ruth M. Porat and Chief Legal Officer Kent Walker. The lawsuit focuses on music AI models including Lyria, Lyria 2, Lyria 3, Mulan and MusicLM, and claims MusicLM, introduced in January 2023, was trained on five million audio clips covering around 280,000 hours of music.

The complaint also accuses Google of using hundreds of thousands of hours of human speech recordings for voice products such as Gemini Live, which it says violated Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act, known as BIPA. That law requires companies to inform people and obtain written permission before collecting biometric data. The lawsuit asks the court to make the defendants pay damages to Alphabet, return their compensation and introduce stronger checks on copyright compliance. The complaint does not mention a specific damages amount.

Separately, Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley wrote to Pichai asking nine questions about how Google's AI tools affect schoolchildren, with a deadline of November 2, 2026 to respond. They said Google is forcing its AI products into classrooms across America and that children are paying the price, and they asked what research Google has done on harms to children's mental health and educational development. The senators cited a Wall Street Journal article that interviewed more than 60 teachers, parents, students and clinicians, and said test scores on national exams have declined and many students are increasingly unable to think critically or complete assignments independently. Their questions also asked about default AI features on licensed education devices, promotional spending in schools, and steps to prevent chatbots from holding sycophantic or emotional conversations with children, including after a Maryland student was hospitalized after developing an intense dependence on Google's AI.

stories.Headline: BigBear.ai vs. Nebius: Which AI Stock Is the Better Buy for 2027?
stories.Summary:
Two Motley Fool articles published in early November 2026 compared BigBear.ai and Nebius Group as AI investments for 2027. John Ballard wrote the comparison, updated on Nov 3, 2026, and David Jagielski wrote a separate piece on BigBear.ai that appeared on Nov 2, 2026. Jagielski's article followed BigBear.ai's third-quarter results, which the company released on Oct. 27, 2026. BigBear.ai reported revenue of $43.6 million for the quarter, up 31%, its third consecutive quarter of organic growth.

BigBear.ai also said it had won more than 25 new deals since the previous quarter, worth over $225 million, and raised its full-year revenue guidance to $150 million to $165 million, a 5% increase over its earlier range. The company posted an operating loss of just under $100 million, mostly because of a $76.7 million goodwill impairment charge, without which the loss would have been $23.2 million. Ballard reported trailing-12-month revenue of nearly $142 million through the June quarter, down about 1.5%, with a net loss of close to $180 million. Nebius, by contrast, reached nearly $1.4 billion in trailing-12-month revenue, up 444%, and net income of $62 million, up from under $10 million for all of 2025.

Ballard said he would buy Nebius over BigBear.ai, arguing that BigBear.ai has a multi-year history of flat revenue, from $146 million in 2021 to $128 million in 2025, with losses across that period. He said Nebius faces immediate demand for its data center capacity and has pricing power, while warning that its stock trades at high multiples and has fallen 38% in the last month on concerns about AI spending. Jagielski said BigBear.ai's results were encouraging but that the business remains risky, citing volatile growth, significant losses and cash burn, and the chance of dilution. He said he would put the stock on a watch list rather than buy it.

Ballard noted that BigBear.ai depends heavily on a limited number of government contracts, which can face budget changes or be terminated at any time. He also reported that BigBear.ai had no debt and a current ratio of about 4.9x, while Nebius carried about $8.6 billion in total debt plus $1.5 billion in lease liabilities against $8 billion in cash. Both companies had negative trailing-12-month free cash flow, at $73 million for BigBear.ai and $5.9 billion for Nebius. Ballard said analysts expect BigBear.ai to keep reporting losses for the next few years and Nebius to keep growing earnings as it brings more capacity online.

stories.Headline: Anthropic's new consulting venture: Why are AI model companies moving into the services business? | Explained
stories.Summary:
Anthropic reportedly plans to set up an AI consultancy in Europe with the private equity firm Hg. The two companies agreed to establish an independent consultancy with hubs in London and Berlin, expected to begin operations by the end of 2026. It is expected to place AI consultants and engineers inside businesses to develop AI-powered products and support adoption. The report said it would also serve companies in Hg's investment portfolio.

The venture reflects a wider shift by AI model companies into work traditionally handled by consulting and IT services firms. This raises questions about who will control enterprise customer relationships and capture revenue from AI implementation. Separately, a Yahoo Finance video said AI is breaking the traditional search business model because people are using AI tools instead of searching on Google and clicking links. The video said this search activity does not generate monetizable search revenue for Google and instead belongs to AI chatbot companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI.

The video pointed to Reddit as an example. It said Reddit announced record earnings with no obvious reason for its stock to fall, yet the stock dropped around 26% in the opening hours of trading. The video said Reddit noted that search ad revenue was not driving enough traffic to its site as usual, and that Google had said a day earlier that AI search does not monetize in the same way. The video also said Reddit is building walls around its service to stop free access, requiring users to create an account and log on, because it fears its company and its large trove of data could be replaced by AI.

The video said Reddit holds an enormous trove of data from comments, subreddits and threads, and that this information is valuable for purchasing decisions, research and news. It said Reddit has given this away for free, while AI companies take the data to train models that effectively become a personal Reddit, without Reddit getting paid. It said Google traditionally drove traffic to Reddit so Reddit could display ads, but if people communicate with the internet through an AI agent or chatbot, there is little reason to visit other websites. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the consultancy's expected start by the end of 2026.

stories.Headline: Tell this AI what you want a protein to do—and it designs one
stories.Summary:
Scientists led by a team at Westlake University in China developed a large-scale AI model called Pinal that can generate candidate proteins from natural language prompts alone, according to a paper published in the journal Nature. A user simply enters a written description of the job they want the protein to do, such as designing a fluorescent protein that emits green light under illumination. Pinal uses two main modules, with the first, T2struct, building a 1D structural blueprint from the description, and the second, SaProt-T, reading that blueprint and using the original text prompt to generate a matching amino acid sequence. The work was reported on November 3, 2026.

Training Pinal required vast amounts of data. The team started with 135 million protein sequences and used AI models and existing protein annotations to build plain-language descriptions of what those proteins do, resulting in a library of 1.7 billion protein-text pairs, and they then obtained predicted 3D structures for those sequences from an existing AlphaFold database. To test Pinal, the researchers asked it to design four different proteins: a fluorescent protein, a plastic-breaking enzyme, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein. For the glowing protein, it created 50,000 sequences, which were filtered down to 29 for testing, and only one actually fluoresced. The system was better at producing the metabolic H-protein shuttle, where five of the 20 candidates worked, and the best one boosted the output of a key carbon-capturing process to 1.7 times that achieved using the natural E. coli protein.

The study authors wrote that Pinal translates high-level functional descriptions into candidate protein sequences, thereby reducing reliance on manually specified structural templates or geometric constraints. The researchers acknowledged that controlling specific properties is still difficult, noting that prompting for a precise emission wavelength in a fluorescent protein remains challenging. They also stated that further work is needed before Pinal becomes a routine lab tool. The article was written by Paul Arnold, edited by Lisa Lock, and fact-checked and reviewed by Robert Egan.

A separate report from BCC Research, released on November 3, 2026, found that AI is improving target selection, sgRNA design, off-target prediction, Cas protein discovery and protein function analysis, helping make CRISPR-based engineering and synthetic biology more precise, efficient and scalable. The report said venture capital investment in AI-related businesses grew from approximately $3 billion in 2012 to $75 billion in 2020, with roughly 20% of all VC deployed that year directed toward AI projects, and that by 2024 corporate AI investment reached $252.3 billion. It said the U.S. led global private AI investment with $109.1 billion in 2024, followed by China at $9.3 billion, while Europe and the U.K. accounted for approximately 4% and 3% respectively. The report also cited Generate Biomedicines raising $400 million in IPO proceeds in 2026 and Profluent raising a $106 million financing round in 2025, bringing total funding to approximately $150 million. It noted headwinds including the EU AI Act's classification of healthcare AI as high-risk, HIPAA and FDA documentation requirements, off-target effects and the validation burden for AI-designed sequences, and said AI adoption is heavily skewed toward North American pharmaceutical and biotech firms, with academic institutions and geographies such as Africa and parts of Latin America at very early stages.

stories.Headline: [PRNewswire] PATEO Advances In-Vehicle AI via NVIDIA Thor
stories.Summary:
PATEO announced on November 3, 2026, that it is advancing in-vehicle AI by deploying NVIDIA Nemotron and the 35-billion-parameter ByteDance Doubao language model in its AI Box, which is built on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. The solution combines local AI inference with PATEO's AI Agent platform to support multilingual interaction, understand cabin context and coordinate vehicle functions. At Auto China 2026 in Beijing, PATEO announced joint development of the solution with ByteDance and a leading new energy vehicle automaker. PATEO has also secured a project nomination for a new-generation vehicle from a leading new energy vehicle automaker, with mass production for that program expected in the second quarter of 2027.

PATEO has integrated NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR for speech recognition into its in-vehicle model suite, and with ByteDance it has integrated Doubao, a 35-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model. The suite also includes text-to-speech synthesis and a 2-billion-parameter language model for semantic classification and request rejection. The integrated suite can run inference locally without a cloud connection, supporting multilingual voice interaction and real-time streaming speech recognition. This keeps core AI functions available when connectivity is limited, while connected services and cloud updates extend the system's capabilities. The AI Agent platform combines voice, visual and sensor inputs to interpret user requests and cabin conditions, and within vehicle safety permissions it can invoke cabin controls and online services, coordinate concurrent tasks and manage longer-running requests.

The AI Box supports scenarios such as Sentinel AI alerts for risks including parking violations, flooding and fire, and separate driver and passenger climate settings by voice or gesture. During extended highway driving, the agent can detect driver fatigue and ask whether the driver would like to open a window or activate seat massage, and in areas with poor air quality it can suggest closing windows and switching to recirculation. Built on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor, the AI Box connects perception, reasoning, execution and learning, and sustaining these experiences requires memory bandwidth alongside peak compute measured in TOPS. By adding dedicated AI computing capacity without replacing the original main control chip, it offers an upgrade path for existing vehicles whose processors cannot support larger models through software updates alone.

PATEO is building on the AI Box to expand from one-time hardware delivery into ongoing AI services, and its in-vehicle Tokenomics strategy aims to create recurring revenue around the deployment and use of AI capabilities. In June 2026, PATEO formed partnerships with Mininglamp Technology, Xunce Technology and Saimo Technology to jointly develop a token-based physical AI world model and TokenOS. The company is also extending its expertise into robotics and reports a project nomination from a leading domestic robotics computing provider. PATEO says its focus on reusable technology, deployment across vehicle programs and ongoing AI services supports its evolution from a smart cockpit supplier into an AI platform company.

stories.Headline: Potential privacy breach at WA mental health facilities after staff member uses ChatGPT
stories.Summary:
Patients at two state-run mental health facilities in Washington may have had their personal health information exposed after a staff member used an unauthorized AI platform to generate medical notes about them. The Lake Burien Transitional Care Facility, which cares for youth with intensive mental health needs, contacted families of a dozen patients in mid-August to inform them of the potential breach. A letter shared with The Seattle Times shows that the Department of Social and Health Services, which oversees Lake Burien, described how an employee reported a colleague was using ChatGPT to draft a summary for client case notes in July. The state then found the employee had used their personal ChatGPT account for other patients. Details including patients' names, diagnosis specifics and medications may have been exposed.

The state said Social Security numbers were not breached and there was no evidence the information had been further disclosed or used for identity theft. DSHS spokesperson Jessica Nelson said the state was aware of one other similar breach, in which four patients at Western State Hospital also had their information potentially exposed. In both cases, Nelson said, staff were notified of DSHS policy around client confidentiality and the use of AI tools. Staff may not use AI without approval from the agency, according to the agency's policy. In the Lake Burien incident, the employee was instructed on IT security protocols and proper care of client confidential information and was told to delete all prompts before deleting their account, which they did.

Taya Briley, an executive vice president for the Washington State Hospital Association, said certain security standards need to be met and none of that will be met if someone is just using ChatGPT on their phone. She said that when hospital staff use a sanctioned AI tool in a medical setting, they must still review and sign off on the notes. Briley said unregulated use of ChatGPT raises concerns when a new technology is introduced and people are not sure of the parameters. She said policies and good AI governance will not be effective if staff are not trained to the extent they need to be. Darcy Jaffe, the association's senior vice president for clinical excellence, said hospitals are being cautious about adopting AI and that there is little external guidance to go on right now.

Bill Howe, an associate professor at the University of Washington's Information School who studies AI, said one option is to move away from frontier models like ChatGPT, Claude and Google Gemini and instead use a system locally controlled by a specific organization. He said he anticipates locally deployed models will become more common. Howe said the other option is to rely on strong legal agreements with the companies that operate these AI platforms, though he noted many companies have violated such agreements and are being sued. He said delivering on the letter of HIPAA law will be increasingly difficult as these systems get more complex. Ruth Schubert, a spokesperson for the Washington State Nurses Association, said in an email that the union has not heard of any similar incidents involving nurses using consumer chatbots for work such as charting patients' information.

stories.Headline: Apple warns of risks related to AI agents behaving in 'unintended or unpredictable' ways
stories.Summary:
Apple said in its annual financial filing on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, that AI agents able to act in unintended or unpredictable ways could threaten its business by opening the company to lawsuits or hurting its reputation. The filing added new risk factors about agents that can take actions autonomously, including interacting with internal or external systems they may not be authorized to access, executing or altering code, sending communications, and completing transactions. Apple wrote that such agents may behave in unintended or unpredictable ways, including by taking actions that were not directed, instructed or authorized. The Fortune report said the filing also warned that rogue agents could conceal actions, hide, withhold or manipulate information, or generate inaccurate or deceptive outputs.

The filing follows several AI safety incidents, including this summer's attack by OpenAI agents on AI company Hugging Face. Earlier this year, OpenAI released an agent called Dots and Meta introduced one called Muse, both of which use advanced AI models to work autonomously. Last month, Apple announced changes to full disk access on Macs to reduce risks related to that level of access for AI agents installed on PCs. Apple also said it does not currently have an agentic AI, and it warned that its ability to oversee and control third-party AI agents may be limited.

Apple chief executive John Ternus, on his first earnings call as CEO on Monday, said agentic capabilities are promising tools for users. He said the company wants to make sure users are aware of what they are giving access to, and that this is done in a way that protects security and privacy. Ternus said Apple cannot access private data on its devices and called that a core differentiator, noting that Siri can tap into personal data such as contacts, communications, health data and financial data in a secure and private way. This fall, Apple released Siri AI, which uses the iPhone's local data storage but cannot work autonomously for long stretches like Dots or Muse.

The filing also outlined other pressures, including memory and storage component shortages that Apple said will intensify. Apple said demand for cloud computing, storage and other AI infrastructure has produced constrained supply, extended lead times and increasing costs that could affect its AI rollout, and its research and development spending rose 32% year over year. Apple shares dropped roughly 2% on Tuesday after the company said its margins would continue to be squeezed by memory chip costs and after it showed slowing growth in its Services segment. Google parent Alphabet also pointed out risks posed by rogue agents in a recent filing, and Microsoft recently announced controls to detect, monitor and restrict AI agents.

stories.Headline: Real people at AI companies may be reading your private chats — here's how to protect yourself
stories.Summary:
OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic all have policies that allow certain conversations with their AI chatbots to be reviewed by humans, according to Tom's Guide. This can happen to improve the AI systems, investigate possible safety violations or troubleshoot problems. The review does not mean someone reads every message, but it does mean chats are not strictly between the user and the chatbot. Deleting a conversation does not always mean every copy is deleted right away. In Google's case, Gemini chats reviewed by humans can stay in company systems for up to three years, even after a user deletes the activity.

When a person types a question into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, the message usually goes to the company's servers, where an AI model processes it and writes a response. Most of that work is automated, but companies also use human reviewers for some conversations. Safety is a major reason, and automated systems flag potentially harmful requests, policy violations and suspicious activity. Some of these interactions may then be passed to a person for review. Fox News reported that ChatGPT has locked chats, which let users protect private conversations with a PIN.

The articles describe the companies involved, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic, as the ones whose policies allow human review. Tom's Guide names Amanda Caswell as the author of its report, published on 3 November 2026, and Fox News published its report on 2 November 2026. The articles do not quote company officials directly. They present the review policies as the companies' own rules and describe the reasons the companies give for them, such as improving their systems, investigating safety violations and troubleshooting problems.

The context is that people often share sensitive things with chatbots, such as medical concerns, relationship problems or documents with financial information. The articles say users should not assume those chats stay private. Tom's Guide offers advice on protecting privacy, and Fox News points to locked chats with a PIN as one way to protect private conversations. The articles do not say what the companies plan to change next.

stories.Headline: [PRNewswire] Cohere Launches Defence AI Accelerator in Singapore
stories.Summary:
Cohere announced on November 3, 2026, that it is establishing a Defence AI Accelerator in Singapore. The accelerator is meant to help defence organizations and other sovereign customers move AI from experimentation to operational deployment in highly secure environments. It will act as a dedicated hub for defence-focused AI innovation, offering hands-on collaboration, technical expertise, and engineering advisory. The goal is to support customers from proof-of-concept through to production systems.

The accelerator is built around practical deployment rather than traditional technology showcases. Participants can experiment with Cohere's models and its agentic AI platform, North, in real-world environments and scale proven solutions into operational infrastructure. Cohere's platform supports on-premises, air-gapped, and hybrid deployments so sovereign customers keep full control over their data and AI infrastructure. Participants get hands-on collaboration with Cohere engineers, secure environments for testing, integration support, and governance frameworks and administrative controls. The announcement is part of Cohere's plans to quadruple its regional presence by the end of 2027 through new investments, local partnerships, and additional offices across APAC.

Andrew Chang, Vice President of APAC at Cohere, said governments and enterprises across the region are moving beyond experimentation and want trusted partners to deploy agentic AI in secure operational environments. He said the accelerator combines Cohere's sovereign AI platform, engineering expertise, and deployment experience to help customers build, test, and scale AI systems that meet high standards for security, governance, and operational reliability. Cohere was founded in 2019 and is headquartered in Toronto, and it operates in cities including Singapore, Seoul, Tokyo, and London. The accelerator will use the North platform, which the company says has already been deployed securely with several regulated organizations in Singapore.

The announcement comes as sovereign AI investment is at an all-time high across APAC. IDC expects 80% of APAC enterprises to prioritize AI sovereignty for mission-critical workloads, and sovereign AI is becoming the region's second-highest government investment priority. The accelerator supports Cohere's goal of expanding support for the public sector in Singapore and strengthening collaboration with public sector institutions. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Cohere's stated plans for regional growth by the end of 2027.

stories.Headline: Meituan Unveils New AI Model Trained on Homegrown Chips
stories.Summary:
Meituan unveiled a new artificial intelligence model called LongCat-2.5 on Monday, November 3, 2026, according to Caixin Global. The on-demand service giant said the model was trained entirely on homegrown chips. It is a native multimodal model trained with 1.6 trillion parameters. Meituan plans to use it to improve efficiency across its core businesses.

The model is designed to handle long-range agent tasks and supports merchant-focused work such as commercial analysis and software development. Benchmark scores place LongCat-2.5 between Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Opus 5, though a developer described the real-world experience as average. Meituan's research and development spending rose 22.5% year on year to 7.7 billion yuan, or about $1.1 billion, in the second quarter of 2026. The company aims its AI at merchant tools rather than selling raw computing power.

CEO Wang Xing said Meituan prioritizes using AI to strengthen its core business instead of selling computing power, according to the article. The report says Meituan's launch shows Chinese tech companies increasingly relying on homegrown chips to advance AI despite hardware limits. It also points to a strategic focus on making money from AI through existing business ecosystems. Other firms are making similar moves, with iFlytek testing domestic chips for model training and Z.AI partly running a 1-gigawatt data center on domestically made chips.

A separate article in The Hindu examines privacy risks in AI training. It says the Supreme Court upheld the right to privacy in 2017, but current legal tools seem inadequate. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was passed in 2023, and its rules were notified in November 2025, with some consent and safety provisions taking effect only in 2027. Before that law, the Information Technology Act of 2000 and its 2011 rules governed personal data, capping penalties for unauthorized disclosure at three years' imprisonment or a fine of 5 lakh rupees.

stories.Headline: Seoul National University of Science and Technology Researchers Develop New AI-Assisted Pipeline to Identify Errors in Construction Design Documents
stories.Summary:
A research team led by Associate Professor Jaewook Jeong from the Department of Safety Engineering at Seoul National University of Science and Technology in South Korea has developed an AI-assisted automated pipeline for detecting human errors in structural design documents. The study was made available online on October 13, 2026, and published in Volume 185 of Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence on December 01, 2026. The work addresses inconsistencies that arise when stakeholders use different tools and formats, which can lead to discrepancies between structural calculation documents and drawings. Such human errors can cause costly delays and, in severe cases, compromise building safety. The pipeline first collects project data and prunes low-quality information, then extracts and standardizes structural information from calculation documents and drawings.

For calculation documents, the DocLayNet-YOLO model identifies regions containing target information, and the Surya-OCR model extracts key structural member data in text form. For drawings, OCR together with Canny edge detection, Hough transform, and morphological operations locates table regions containing member codes, which are then filtered, refined, and standardized. Using member codes and directions as identifiers, the system cross-validates the two document types, detects errors, and flags duplicates, and the researchers deployed it through a user-friendly, web-based application. In a case study of a residential construction project in South Korea, the system reached extraction accuracies of 95.56% for structural calculation documents and 90.47% for structural drawing documents. Verification identified 253 discrepancies, including 224 missing entries, 18 reinforcement mismatches, eight dimensional discrepancies, and three duplicates.

Jeong said the framework automatically extracts, organizes, and compares information to identify inconsistencies that may result from human error, and that it performs these checks without relying on BIM. He noted that the pipeline could help structural engineers, design consultants, contractors, and construction supervision teams find discrepancies before they lead to construction errors. The researchers describe the framework as particularly valuable for small- and medium-sized construction projects that cannot implement BIM, which is limited by high initial costs, a lack of skilled personnel, and technical barriers. The system could reduce the burden of manual checking and improve consistency in projects where BIM cannot be implemented. According to the articles, it could in the future be integrated into routine engineering workflows, making advanced safety technologies more accessible.

stories.Headline: VivoSim Labs and Chemveda Life Sciences Join Forces to Put AI-Designed Drug Candidates to the Human Test
stories.Summary:
VivoSim Labs and Chemveda Life Sciences announced a strategic collaboration on November 3, 2026, to test AI-designed drug compounds in human tissue models. VivoSim is based in San Diego and trades on Nasdaq under the symbol VIVS. Chemveda is an integrated contract research, development and manufacturing organization founded in 2008 by Dr. Bheema Rao Paraselli. The two companies said the deal closes the gap between AI drug design and human biology.

Under the collaboration, Chemveda will design, synthesize, optimize and develop AI-designed compounds for pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients. VivoSim will then evaluate selected compounds using its NAMkind Liver and NAMkind Intestine models, which are built from primary human cells. VivoSim's screens can evaluate more than 20 compounds in two weeks. In a clinical dataset of 92 small-molecule compounds, the NAMkind Liver model predicted drug-induced liver injury with 91% accuracy, 90% sensitivity and 95% specificity. The joint offering will be available to Chemveda's global client base, with first programs expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Keith Murphy, Executive Chairman of VivoSim, said AI has given the industry a flood of new molecules but not a way to know which will work and which may harm patients. He said the collaboration lets partners know in weeks, not years, which molecules deserve to move forward. Dr. Bheema Rao Paraselli, founder, President and Chief Executive Officer of Chemveda, said his company was founded to shorten the distance between an idea and a molecule. He said combining Chemveda's chemistry capabilities with VivoSim's models creates a tighter feedback loop, so clients can spot liabilities earlier and feed insights back to chemists.

The companies said liver and gastrointestinal toxicity remain among the most common reasons promising drugs fail in the clinic, often after years of work and hundreds of millions of dollars. They also noted that the collaboration arrives as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration actively encourages human-relevant new approach methodologies in place of animal testing. Chemveda has more than 600 employees and a global footprint spanning India, San Diego and Dundee, Scotland. Companies interested in screening AI-derived compounds can contact either company.

stories.Headline: Cat Wu, product lead for Claude Code and Cowork, has left Anthropic; Thariq Shihipar, who worked on Claude Code, announced his departure last month (Stephen Council/Business Insider)
stories.Summary:
Cat Wu, who led product for Claude Code and Cowork at Anthropic, left the company on Friday, November 1, 2026. She announced her departure on X on Tuesday afternoon, thanking the Claude Code team and its users. Anthropic confirmed her departure. Thariq Shihipar, who also worked on Claude Code, announced his own departure last month. Wu did not say what prompted her to leave and did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Wu joined Anthropic in summer 2024 and tested an early prototype of Claude Code. Anthropic released the tool in a research preview in February 2025, with a demo video featuring Wu and Boris Cherny, Claude Code's original creator. Wu and Cherny left for the AI coding startup Cursor that summer and returned to Anthropic a couple of weeks later, according to The Information. Wu was one of the two top leaders and evangelists for Claude Code alongside Cherny, and she also oversaw Cowork, Anthropic's tool for non-coding work.

In an April interview on Lenny's Podcast, Wu described her role as figuring out how to bring Claude Code to the "AGI-pilled" version Cherny envisioned. She said she worked with marketing, sales, finance, and other teams and hired some of Anthropic's product managers. She also regularly answered user requests about Claude Code on social media. When one commenter asked under her X post whether she would take a six-month vacation, Wu replied, "post agi!"

Wu leaves at a crucial moment, as Anthropic moves toward a large initial public offering later this month. Under Wu and Cherny, Claude Code became one of the most important products in the AI industry's history, giving Anthropic a viral product that boosted its revenues and helped it raise more funding for compute. The tool first grew popular as an automatic coder for software engineers, and tech giants' AI bills with Anthropic soared as more developers used Claude tokens. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the planned IPO.

stories.Headline: OpenAI introduces program to reduce AI data center energy demand during peak hours
stories.Summary:
OpenAI introduced a program called the Grid Protectors Program on November 3, 2026, to reduce the electricity demand of its data centers when the local grid is under strain. The company is testing the system at its planned Effingham County campus in Georgia. OpenAI said the program aims to cut power use as local demand rises, so the grid is not overwhelmed during peak hours. The company also said the effort could let its data centers connect and go online sooner instead of waiting for more power sources.

OpenAI has signed a 3.2-gigawatt agreement with Georgia Power that includes 1,000 megawatts of flexible demand response. The company said the 1,000-megawatt buffer is more than enough to power around 800,000 households, nearly 20% of the state's homes. OpenAI said US data center capacity is projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030. The program is described as non-binding, and OpenAI called the effort an ambition rather than a set policy. The company said arrangements will differ by location and that it will share more commitments as they are finalized.

OpenAI said families need reliable electricity, whether it is heating homes during a northern cold snap or running air conditioning through a southern heat wave. The company said its goal is to make campus flexibility a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most. OpenAI said it plans to work with utilities, regulators, and policymakers, and that the program could include on-site generation or storage and batteries and power controls to smooth demand fluctuations. Kim Greene, chairman, president and CEO of Georgia Power, said data centers are paying more so families and small businesses can pay less, and that the goal of every contract under the framework is to deliver value for them.

Demand response has been around for decades, with grid operators once calling industrial customers like steel mills to ask them to cut consumption. Modern technology and IoT now let data centers reduce their load in under a minute, and Nvidia has already been experimenting with a similar system in the UK and has shown that it works. OpenAI said it has committed to paying the full cost of the infrastructure required to serve its Georgia Power data center. The articles do not say what happens next beyond OpenAI sharing additional commitments as they are finalized.

stories.Headline: Siri AI opens to third-party apps in iOS 27.3 beta
stories.Summary:
Apple began beta testing iOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, watchOS 27.3 and other updates on November 3, 2026, after iOS 27.2 reached customers on October 26. A highlight of the beta is that Apple now allows all developers to connect their apps to Siri AI using App Intents. The betas also bring two Audio Intelligence features to the latest Apple Watch models, Live Rewind and Siri Recap, and they bring back Apple's redesigned Health app. Apple Intelligence tools also arrive in China with this update, though Siri AI does not.

Apple said the preview lets any app bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness and natural language. Users will be able to check a delivery, book a reservation or place an order without opening an app, and developers can teach Siri to combine several actions for more complicated requests. The new capabilities are available for testing in the betas, with apps expected to begin reaching customers in 2027. Submissions to the App Store using the new capabilities are open until spring, and Apple says iOS 27.3 will reach the public in December.

On Apple's earnings call on November 2, chief financial officer Kevan Parekh said AI offers a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch, and that there are opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships as well as first-party opportunities. He did not elaborate on what those opportunities might be, and Reuters reported that investors are wondering whether Apple could profit by distributing third-party AI agents through the App Store and taking a cut of the revenue. Parekh said App Store performance in the September quarter was similar to the prior year, with a record number of paid subscriptions and double-digit growth for third-party apps, but he noted headwinds in mobile gaming. He said services growth is expected to be between 8 and 9 percent in the December quarter.

Apple has been talking up third-party access to Siri AI since WWDC26 in June, and the beta is the first step toward it. The first beta is available to registered developers through Software Update in Settings, and a public beta should follow the developer release. The Audio Intelligence features work only on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 because they depend on a hardware-isolated Secure Exclave in the new S11 processor. The redesigned Health app adds an Insights tab with personalized recommendations and a Longevity section with a Health Age estimate, and it had been pulled from later iOS 27.2 betas before the public release.

stories.Headline: OpenAI Introduces Pando: A Git Backend That Cuts Median Push Latency ~80%
stories.Summary:
OpenAI introduced Pando, a new Git backend that now serves all development in its monorepo, the company announced on November 3, 2026. Pando is written in Rust and reached production in 10 weeks, with one engineer designing the core and teams of Codex agents implementing it. It has served production traffic since April 2026. Engineers and Codex agents still run git push and git fetch as before, and only the server changed.

OpenAI reports that median push latency fell nearly 80%, about 5x, and that Pando delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day, with peak traffic above 57 TB in one hour. It runs on commodity hardware, and standard cloud VMs saturate 10 Gbps links on clone and fetch. OpenAI says thousands of concurrent pushers work without degradation in its own testing. Pando is not open source, and repeat branch pushes resend non-trunk history, with a p99 pack under 3 MiB.

Pando uses causal consistency, so each branch is serialized on its own and clients only conflict when pushing the same ref, though a reader viewing several branches may see them at different points in time. Each pushed pack is stored as an immutable blob, and a ref version goes into a scalable metadata store. Pando advertises only the trunk branch as the base for new feature-branch pushes, and in OpenAI's monorepo the median pack was under 20 KiB. It returns download links via packfile-uri, an existing Git protocol feature, and a delivery service called Express caches packs regionally with hit rates above 99%.

OpenAI says its commit chart shows commits landed on master up 1,378% in Q3 2026 versus Q1 2024, with a Q4 2026 estimate of +2,442%. By late 2025, fetches and pushes slowed, merges failed, and reliability at times fell below 90%, and OpenAI concluded the bottleneck was how it served Git, not Git itself. Each push creates an L0 pack, and background workers group packs into geometrically larger covers, similar to LSM-tree compaction, with the monorepo currently using covers up to L4. OpenAI also ran a 1,000-writer simulation against 3-phase-commit and write-ahead-log designs, which it labels teaching models, not benchmarks.

stories.Headline: Biren urges Manipur home dept to make public biometric data on illegal immigrants
stories.Summary:
Former Manipur chief minister N Biren Singh urged the state home department on Tuesday to share updated information on the biometric enrolment of illegal immigrants. He made the appeal in a social media post, saying regular disclosure would strengthen public confidence and reaffirm the government's commitment to the state's security. His remarks came after the government in neighbouring Mizoram said the biometric enrolment of Myanmar refugees sheltering there was in its final phase. Mizoram has covered 99.90% of the 29,792 Myanmar nationals currently in the state, with only 33 individuals yet to be registered.

Singh said the issue was not about politics but about national security, safeguarding borders and protecting the future of the people. He said the Mizoram government had shown the importance of vigilance by closely monitoring the influx of illegal immigrants and taking measures to protect the state's interests. He added that it would be in the public interest for the Manipur home department to regularly share updated information on biometric data collected, including the number of individuals identified and verified. He said such transparency would strengthen public confidence and reaffirm the government's commitment to protecting the state's security and the interests of its indigenous communities.

Home minister Konthoujam Govindas told the assembly last September that 24,475 illegal immigrants from Myanmar had been detected in Manipur. Of these, 14,992 have returned to Myanmar and 9,453 are staying in temporary shelters in border districts. He added that in Chandel, biometrics have been taken of 1,308 of the 4,770 immigrants who remain. Manipur shares 390 km of India's 1,634 km border with Myanmar, and most stretches remain unfenced, which has allegedly aided illegal migration and cross-border crime.

Mizoram and Manipur saw an influx of Myanmar nationals who fled after the military launched a crackdown on pro-democracy protesters in 2021. More than 35,000 Myanmar refugees have been sheltered in neighbouring Mizoram, and the Union home ministry subsequently directed Manipur and Mizoram to record biometric details of suspected illegal immigrants. The biometric exercise in Manipur began when Biren Singh was in office, and a cabinet sub-committee was set up in February 2023 to identify illegal immigrants. The Manipur campaign resumed in July 2023 after being disrupted by the ethnic violence that broke out on May 3, and the Centre extended the deadline for the state to complete the exercise from September 30, 2023, by six months to March 31, 2024. In May 2024, Singh, then chief minister, said biometric data of 5,173 of the 5,457 illegal immigrants found in Kamjong district had been collected.

stories.Headline: Fewer jobs, new opportunities: AI is changing what’s in store for new hires and managers alike.
stories.Summary:
Northeastern University’s AI & Society Survey found that AI is screening résumés and changing hiring. The report examined responses from 8,174 people who said they have a say in who gets hired. Roughly half said AI made a difference in their decisions. Among them, 26% said they were hiring fewer entry-level candidates, while only 7% said they were hiring more.

The rest reported steady hiring rates but were divided in their expectations, with 28% expecting more output or higher-level work from entry-level employees. AI is on résumé duty for 54% of hiring decision-makers, and in tech that figure reaches 83%. Around 38% said a college degree makes a candidate more valuable, and about one in five said it is much more valuable. Almost half said AI experience was not explicitly on their radar, and around 40% see AI use for every writing or coding assignment as a plus, while 21% said it would discourage them from making an offer.

John Wihbey, a Northeastern professor of media and communications technology and a co-author of the survey, said the fears around entry-level jobs are real. He suggested that AI use would increase demand for the critical thinking a college education instills, and that there is a demand for graduates who have AI fluency and readiness. Gary Friedman, a New York employment trial lawyer at Seyfarth Shaw, said AI can hollow out the bottom rung of the ladder or turn it into an escalator. He added that an algorithm can make thousands of errors in a nanosecond and that AI won’t replace human judgment.

The report is the latest in a series that opened with an analysis of how people across the political spectrum view AI training. Hiring decision-makers were almost twice as likely as respondents in other roles to expect AI to make them more productive, and around 7 in 10 felt more AI training would be useful. They were also twice as likely to say that most or all of their work could be outsourced to AI. Northeastern offers a five-course AI minor open to students without a programming background, 24 combined majors pairing AI with other subjects and AI-focused co-ops.

stories.Headline: AMD’s AI Boom Puts It On Track To Outsell Intel For The First Time – Analysts See More Room To Grow
stories.Summary:
On November 3, 2026, AMD reported third-quarter results and forecast fourth-quarter sales that would top Intel's, putting it on track to outsell Intel for the first time in their history if both companies meet their targets. AMD's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to a record $13.4 billion, with data center sales nearly doubling from a year earlier to $8.5 billion, or 64% of overall revenue, up from 47% a year before. AMD guided fourth-quarter sales at about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, above analysts' target of $16.3 billion and above Intel's forecast of $15 billion to $16 billion. Intel's third-quarter sales rose 21% to $16.5 billion, in line with expectations, with $7.3 billion in data center sales.

The results follow Intel's weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter forecast and its warning about continuing weakness in the PC market, which sent Intel shares down more than 20% in a day last week. Intel CFO David Zinsner said the company expects the PC slowdown to continue at least through the first half of next year. AMD also said it expects sales to grow 80% in 2027 on demand for data center chips, and it outlined gains from partnerships with big AI companies and strong sales of new products such as Helios and Venice. AMD recently deepened its partnership with Meta Platforms, planning to invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering and deploy Helios rack-scale AI computing systems at Meta data centers, where initial systems are installed and being tested.

AMD CFO Lisa Su said on the analyst call that the third quarter was the largest and most profitable in the company's history as it began ramping next-generation data center products. Nicholas Mugalli, CEO of World Trade Securities, said in an X post that AMD was a scrappy underdog a few years ago and now its quarter is bigger than Intel's whole business, adding that AMD guided well above the Street while Intel is stuck in PCs. The Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman said in an X post that AMD has a history of under promising and over delivering with its guides and he sees more of the same. Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis kept a Buy rating and a $650 price target, and Susquehanna analyst Christopher Rolland also kept a Buy rating, expecting AMD's data center GPU revenue to reach about $41 billion in 2027 and total data center revenue of $74 billion, above the $71 billion consensus.

Ahead of the report, AMD shares fell as investors weighed Intel's PC warning against the Meta AI work, with the stock near $477.84 on Monday afternoon, down $26.96, or 5.34%, from the previous close of $504.80. AMD stock fell over 17% in the final two days of last week following Intel's earnings, and as of its last close it had run 126% higher year to date. The options market was pricing an 8.95% move, or about $45.17 per share, in either direction around the earnings report. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for AMD shifted from extremely bullish to bullish, while sentiment for Intel remained extremely bullish for a second day.

stories.Headline: Deepfake AI Market to Grow at 47.93% CAGR Through 2031 Driven by Rising Synthetic Media and Fraud Detection Demand, Says Mordor Intelligence
stories.Summary:
Mordor Intelligence published a report on the deepfake AI market on November 3, 2026, from Hyderabad, India. The study says the market was valued at USD 1.66 billion in 2026 and is projected to reach USD 11.76 billion by 2031. That works out to a compound annual growth rate of 47.93% over the forecast period from 2026 to 2031. The report covers market dynamics, technology trends, the competitive landscape, and future opportunities.

The study links growth to advances in generative artificial intelligence, rising demand for synthetic media, increasing deepfake-enabled financial fraud, and growing investment in detection technologies. It names generative adversarial networks, transformer models, and multimodal artificial intelligence as forces speeding up growth. Organizations are adopting the technology for synthetic media creation, content personalization, identity verification, fraud prevention, and media authentication. The report also lists restraints, including regulatory uncertainty, fragmented legal frameworks, high computational costs, eroding consumer trust, and a shortage of diverse training data.

Ashish Gautam, a Senior Research Manager at Mordor Intelligence, said organizations and technology providers need research that separates the expanding uses of synthetic media from the growing requirements for detection, authentication, and responsible AI governance. He said the firm combines extensive primary research with rigorous secondary analysis to give balanced, evidence-based insights. He said these support informed business decisions across rapidly evolving artificial intelligence markets. The report also names companies profiled in the competitive landscape, including Synthesia Limited, D-ID Ltd., Reality Defender Inc., Microsoft Corp., Google LLC, Amazon Web Services Inc., and NVIDIA Corporation.

North America continues to lead the market, supported by established AI ecosystems, enterprise adoption in entertainment and financial services, government investment, and demand for digital authentication. The United States remains a major market for both synthetic-media applications and deepfake detection solutions. Asia Pacific is expected to see strong growth, backed by government AI investments, expanding digital infrastructure, edge computing adoption, and a growing provider ecosystem. China, India, Japan, and South Korea are named as creating opportunities in generation, detection, authentication, and responsible AI applications.
