stories.Headline: OC students to lead AI workshops, showcase innovations at Nov. 6 convening
stories.Summary:
The Orange County Department of Education will hold its third annual Student AI Convening on Friday, Nov. 6, at the OCDE Conference Center in Costa Mesa. The free event runs from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. in Building D at 200 Kalmus Drive. It is designed and led by students and will feature an opening keynote, six interactive breakout sessions and a closing program.

Students from communities including Santa Ana, Tustin, Costa Mesa, Huntington Beach, Fountain Valley and La Habra are expected to attend. The keynote is titled “The Future Isn’t Just Something We Inherit. It’s Something We Shape,” and will be given by Aahan Jain of El Toro High School and Jazzy Mancilla of Costa Mesa High School. Denise Duong of Fountain Valley High School will introduce machine learning using Teachable Machine, a web-based tool for creating AI models without coding experience. Pradyumn Singh of Kennedy High School will present Wisteria, a tool to help students organize Advanced Placement exam preparation through personalized schedules.

Ollie Rankin of Laguna Beach High School will demonstrate an educational game called Storyscape and introduce participants to vibe coding, and other sessions will cover how AI processes human language, critical thinking and recognizing bias. Each breakout session will be offered twice. Wes Kriesel, OCDE’s AI education lead, said the convening is a must-attend because students did not just plan it but are running it. He said the keynote, every breakout and the closing are led by students for students. He said that when a high schooler teaches peers how neural networks work, or demos an AI tutor built for their own district, that is students shaping the future right now.

He said that is the experience they want for every student in Orange County. The convening is an extension of OCDE’s Student AI Network, which connects middle and high school students across Orange County to explore artificial intelligence, share projects and learn from one another. The network is led by Kriesel and welcomes students of all experience levels who are curious about AI. More information about the event, including student presenters and session descriptions, is available on the 2026 Student AI Convening webpage. Students interested in joining the network can learn more through the OC Student AI Network.

Articles.Title: OC students to lead AI workshops, showcase innovations at Nov. 6 convening

stories.Headline: Why F1’s rule-makers are turning to AI to keep up with the teams and close loopholes
stories.Summary:
The Formula 1 governing body, the FIA, has chosen Amazon Web Services as its new partner for artificial intelligence, cloud computing, machine learning, and cloud infrastructure, an announcement made on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The move follows the F1 organization's own work with AWS, which began in 2018, and comes as all 11 teams have already announced partnerships with AI firms. The FIA writes the final rulebook and polices how cars must look and perform aerodynamically, so the new deal is aimed at its own technical work. AWS already helped shape car design rules for the 2022 and 2026 regulation cycles.

The partnership gives the FIA more access to AWS capabilities, including newer and better hardware, while reducing costs. AWS's head of motorsport, Michael Aghataher, said the approach lets the FIA run thousands of simulations in parallel, turning a process that once took months into one that can finish in hours. The FIA is also looking at AI for policing track limits, with a road map to expand its use over the next couple of years. Under that plan, a human would still make each call, while AI pulls the needed data points and camera footage. Each F1 car carries 300 sensors that produce 1.1 million data points per second, or 24 million data points per race, which the FIA also hopes to process faster with AI.

The FIA's single-seater deputy technical director, Dominic Harlow, said AI is among the top interests for engineers right now and framed the effort as a way to keep pace with the teams. He said the teams are working hard to find loopholes in the rules, and that the FIA's technical department faces larger staff groups at each team. Aghataher described AWS as a supporting tool that optimizes human performance rather than a replacement for people. Harlow also said generative AI in car design regulation was something the FIA could imagine in the future, but that the work remains human-driven for now.

AI is now a regular agenda item at F1 Commission meetings, which set the rules and include the teams, the FIA and the F1 organization. Harlow said the sport is still in an exploration phase and has not yet made a large deployment or a real shift in how people work. The FIA plans to keep discussing the technology and monitor how it affects the areas that matter most to the sport. Given F1's long positioning at the leading edge of technology, all parties are watching closely how AI will be put into practice.

Articles.Title: Why F1’s rule-makers are turning to AI to keep up with the teams and close loopholes - The New York Times

stories.Headline: AI Hallucination Sanctions in 2026: 13 Verified Cases in One Table
stories.Summary:
In 2026 courts in the United States, England and Wales imposed sanctions in cases involving AI-fabricated material, and a table verified 13 notable rulings against court orders or major legal press. The largest total was about $110,000 in Couvrette v. Wisnovsky in Oregon, where the fine was about $15,500 and the rest was opposing counsel's fees. The harshest outcomes were suspensions, dismissals and a default judgment, not fines. The table was published on 3 November 2026 and drew on Damien Charlotin's AI Hallucination Cases database, which listed 2,262 decisions worldwide, 1,533 of them from the United States, when updated on 2 November 2026.

The rulings ran from 5 February 2026, when a default judgment was entered in Flycatcher Corp. v. Affable Avenue LLC in the Southern District of New York, to 28 July 2026, when the Illinois Appellate Court fined a lawyer $15,000 at $1,500 per false citation or quotation in Scott v. Illinois Human Rights Commission. The Sixth Circuit ordered $15,000 each for two lawyers in Whiting v. City of Athens on 13 March 2026, plus appeal fees, double costs and a disciplinary referral, with no finding that AI was used.

The Ninth Circuit gave $2,500 each and six months' suspension from that court to two lawyers in Lnu v. Blanche on 3 June 2026. In Withers v. City of Aberdeen on 8 June 2026, $8,000 was spread across four lawyers on both sides, all were disqualified, two were barred from the district for two years and the trial was cancelled. The article says courts punish the cover-up as much as the error, and it lists lack of candour, failed supervision, signing what you did not read and repetition as recurring factors.

In Gentry v. Thompson the supervising lawyer paid $1,000 and the drafter $250, and in Cork v Smith the High Court of England and Wales publicly admonished a firm and two solicitors, with the firm self-reporting to the SRA. Magistrate Judge Mark Clarke called Couvrette a notorious outlier in both degree and volume, and the Sixth Circuit said smaller fines have plainly been inadequate. The Fifth Circuit said a lawyer using generative AI must ensure that the legal propositions and authority generated are trustworthy.

The article says clients often pay, because Flycatcher ended in a default judgment, Couvrette was dismissed with prejudice and the appeal in Ibach v. Stewart was dismissed. It says the true number of incidents is unknown because many errors are never caught, and that the table is a selection, not a complete list. It says rows will be added as more orders are reported.

Articles.Title: AI Hallucination Sanctions in 2026: 13 Verified Cases in One Table - Legal Desire

stories.Headline: President Donald Trump announces creation of 'Super Intelligence Force' AI task force
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump formally announced the creation of what he called a "Super Intelligence Force," an artificial intelligence task force, ABC30 reported. The announcement came in a post on his social media platform on Sunday, October 4, 2026, and was reported the next day by Emily Chang. Trump said the force will work to promote AI dominance while protecting American lives and interests. The announcement was thin on details, and the White House did not immediately respond to an ABC News request for more information. Trump wrote that the force is tasked with coordinating the federal government's effort to keep America leading the world in super intelligence.

He said it will coordinate engagement with consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers and super intelligence companies. The task force will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, along with Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor. The formal announcement followed a White House meeting with top tech CEOs last week, where Trump said he and six companies signed a "constitution" setting standards for self-policing their technology. Clayton, who is expected to serve as the White House's new AI czar, told The Wall Street Journal that global dominance in AI makes the U.S. better equipped to address risks from adversaries. He said the risk of not being first is high and that being first will better enable the country to address those risks for the American people.

He said he expects mechanisms to be developed in dialogue, like in other industries, and cited risk models for the financial industry developed with the Federal Reserve and Securities and Exchange Commission. Clayton also said the task force would examine current law and discuss possible actions Congress could take, and he expressed confidence in the group's diverse skill sets and common commitment. The announcement comes amid rising concerns about artificial intelligence, and some tech CEOs have called for federal regulation. Last month, Trump said he would create an AI task force amid those concerns. The articles do not say what specific action or oversight the task force will have over AI development.

Articles.Title: President Donald Trump announces creation of 'Super Intelligence Force' AI task force

stories.Headline: China Prepares to Impose New Safety Standards for AI Firms
stories.Summary:
China is reportedly preparing to set wide-ranging safety standards for artificial intelligence, according to a Bloomberg News report on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The report cites comments from China’s economic planner, which said it is ramping up legislation to govern how AI is developed and applied, from development to deployment. The measures would be among the most thorough guidelines to protect against a loss of control as AI becomes more powerful. The regulations would extend to areas such as data and computing power, according to Wang Ruomeng, a senior official with the National Development and Reform Commission.

The rules would cover companies such as DeepSeek, Moonshot and Alibaba as they try to compete against U.S. rivals OpenAI and Anthropic. Wang said at a briefing in Beijing that the government will accelerate legislation to support core AI enablers, including data, computing power and algorithms, and regulate key application scenarios. He said the government will establish safety standards and ethical guidelines covering the full life cycle of AI. He added that the government will conduct regular reviews of how the rules are carried out and revise guidelines that become outdated.

Wang also said China will keep an eye on AI’s impact on employment and displacement and provide protections for affected workers. At the same time, he said the government will keep encouraging AI development. He called on countries to cooperate on protections around the technology, saying AI safety is not a problem one company, industry or country can tackle alone and is a global challenge requiring international cooperation. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the planned legislation and reviews.

Articles.Title: China Prepares to Impose New Safety Standards for AI Firms

stories.Headline: Trump says he will form new 'AI Force' but continues to call AI fears a 'hoax'
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump said on Saturday, September 19, 2026, that he would move to create a new "AI Force" and promised to appoint an AI czar in the near future. He made the announcement in a post on social media, likening the force to Space Force, which was created during his first term. Trump also continued to call fears about AI alignment a "hoax." It is unclear what the "AI Force" would be tasked with doing, and the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump said the U.S. would form the "AI Force" to look out for the "bad" aspects of AI. He said another armed forces branch would require further action from Congress, and Space Force itself was created by an act of Congress in 2020 as a sixth branch under the Department of Defense. Trump said the U.S. could already handle bad actors "very easily" through the existing criminal and civil justice system. He also said his administration would not hinder or stifle the growth of the industry, and that it would cherish, help and watch over it as it grows.

Trump's comments came after warnings from top tech leaders about the potential dangers of AI. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a blog post last week calling to slow the pace of AI development, and shortly afterward OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said his company would welcome a slower pace so capabilities don't get ahead of alignment and monitoring. Some lawmakers have also called for more guardrails around AI development. Trump responded at the time that the warnings were a "HOAX" and that there was a "SICK conspiracy" going on around AI.

David Sacks, co-chair of Trump's science and technology council, indicated at a Politico conference on Wednesday that more regulations were not necessarily needed. Sacks, who previously served as the White House's former AI and crypto czar until stepping down in March, said the starting point for talking about AI regulation is to realize the regulations that already exist. He said there is a highly regulated administrative state, with many laws and regulations that pertain to AI and many agencies that promulgate them. The articles do not say what happens next beyond Trump's promise to name an AI czar in the near future.

Articles.Title: Trump says he will form new 'AI Force' but continues to call AI fears a 'hoax' - ABC13 Houston

stories.Headline: Garland County Library board approves AI policy, change order for new branch - Hot Springs Sentinel Record
stories.Summary:
The Garland County Library Board of Trustees voted on Monday afternoon to establish an artificial intelligence policy for library employees, the Hot Springs Sentinel Record reported. The board also approved a change order for the new North Garland County branch during the same meeting. Executive Director Adam Webb discussed a pair of change orders for the branch at the meeting. The vote came amid the rise of artificial intelligence.

The policy does not require employees to use AI, but it sets guidelines for employees who might use it as part of their workflow. The article gives no further numbers, dates or names beyond the Monday meeting, Webb and the branch. The report was published on Nov. 3, 2026, by James Leigh. The meeting took place Monday afternoon.

Webb discussed the change orders for the new North Garland County branch during the trustees meeting. The article does not say what the change orders involve or what they change about the branch project. It also does not give the vote count or say who else spoke. The reporting is subscriber-exclusive coverage from the Sentinel-Record.

The article does not describe the context beyond the rise of artificial intelligence. It does not say what happens next with the policy or the branch change orders. No next steps, timelines or future meetings are given. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Garland County Library board approves AI policy, change order for new branch - Hot Springs Sentinel Record

stories.Headline: UNESCO, Brazilian Government and ITU partner to launch green AI Climate Institute
stories.Summary:
UNESCO, the Government of Brazil and the International Telecommunication Union formed a partnership to establish the Artificial Intelligence Climate Institute, known as AICI. The institute was announced at COP30 in Belém on 11 November 2025, and its vision was set out there. On 4 August 2026, an inaugural workshop in Manaus, Brazil, hosted by Anatel and the UNESCO Brasília Office, finalized the institute's operational structure. The founding partners plan to officially launch the AICI operational phase at COP31 in Antalya on 16 November 2026.

The institute is hosted by Brazil's National Telecommunications Agency, Anatel, within its Green Digital Action Hub in Brasília, and it sits under ITU's Green Digital Action Hub. It works through a two-year roadmap for 2026 to 2027 focused on country-led capacity building. Training is split into executive tracks on data governance and climate policy for public officials and hands-on engineering labs for local developers and data scientists. A shared digital learning repository will hold open-access environmental datasets, climate-specific model architectures and green prompting guidelines for low-connectivity, resource-constrained settings, and developing economies are meant to keep data sovereignty and the technical independence to train, fine-tune and maintain local climate models.

Under the partnership, Brazil through Anatel provides institutional hosting for the AICI Secretariat and steers regional cooperation. The ITU supplies technical expertise in telecommunications and digital infrastructure and links the work with the ITU Academy and the AI Skills Coalition. UNESCO grounds the curriculum and projects in its 2021 Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and its Open Science framework. Guilherme Canela de Souza Godoi, Director of UNESCO's Division for Digital Inclusion and Policies and Digital Transformation, said the institute connects the rapid advance of artificial intelligence with the urgency of tackling climate change, and that sustainable AI must be inclusive and reach countries and communities with different levels of capacity.

The institute is meant to help developing nations, especially in the Global South, overcome restricted computing capacity, fragmented data governance and technical skills gaps. It operationalizes Objective 4 of the COP29 Declaration on Green Digital Action, expanding digital inclusion, literacy and skills development for climate resilience. UNESCO cites a joint UNESCO-UCL study showing that task-specific models and optimized prompts can reduce AI energy consumption by up to 90 percent, and it deploys modules through networks including the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme and Man and the Biosphere reserves. At the Antalya launch, the partners will unveil the approved 2026-2027 work plan, showcase scalable pilot applications including AI-driven deforestation prevention in the Amazon Basin, and formally open membership to governments, research institutions and international financing partners.

Articles.Title: UNESCO, Brazilian Government and ITU partner to launch green AI Climate Institute

stories.Headline: AI alters ITAD economics
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is spreading through the technology asset recovery sector, changing how equipment is inspected, valued and sent to reuse or material recovery. Established and startup companies are investing in automated systems that identify devices, assess their condition and recommend what to do with them. Some platforms add fair market value data to offer end-to-end services the author calls orchestration software. Many of these systems can produce records that once required extensive manual work. The commercial effects go beyond lower labor costs, because more consistent grading can affect resale prices and earlier asset information can improve refurbishment and remarketing decisions.

Sage Sustainable Electronics’ 2026 IT Asset Management Benchmarking Report found that average enterprise laptop refresh cycles shortened from 4.3 to 4.0 years. Server resale values in 2025 reached nearly 2.5 times their seven-year average, reflecting constrained component supply and demand tied to AI infrastructure. The study draws on 56 organizations representing more than 808,000 employees, plus processing data covering more than 2.5 million IT assets between 2019 and 2025. Reconext has developed proprietary systems that combine automated testing with AI-assisted visual inspection. Its Pegasus platform uses optical recognition to identify products and read part numbers while creating image-supported receiving records, and Optiline applies image recognition to cosmetic grading.

Reconext’s Proteus platform supports storage-device diagnostics and data erasure, with configurations accommodating up to 64 test cells, and Phoenix tests as many as 10 DDR3 or DDR4 memory modules in parallel. Reconext describes its systems as commercially deployable, including installations within partner facilities, but public descriptions do not provide independently verified comparisons of processing costs or net resale proceeds against conventional operations. Ingram Micro’s Lifecycle business combines asset valuation with recovery services, while its Xvantage platform supports digital coordination across the technology distribution and services ecosystem. Microsoft reported that its Circular Centers reused more than 3.2 million components in 2024, and internally harvested inventory fulfilled 85% of demand for obsolete spare parts no longer manufactured. Microsoft also reported a 90.9% reuse and recycling rate for servers and cloud hardware components in 2024, exceeding its 2025 target one year early.

Exact Asset, formerly Vision Intel, combines autonomous inspection systems with RFID-based asset tracking and pricing technology, and it offers autonomous scanning tunnels that inspect returned equipment without manual intervention. Exact Asset reports that automated grading can increase resale values by more than 25%, while its broader asset intelligence offering advertises improvements in return on investment of up to 70%. G2 Reverse Logistics applies AI directly to commercial decisions, shifting from retrospective fair market value to dynamic market state residual value, which factors in live market demand, real-time processing friction, configuration health and logistics overhead. Its DecisionAI evaluates asset economics against live macroeconomic signals, while ResaleIQ identifies optimal resale and liquidation channels, and its Returns Management System directs floor technicians whether to redeploy, refurbish, wholesale or harvest components. Blancco Technology Group announced Blancco Blue in October, an agentic platform that introduces conversational AI into operational workflows and includes Ask Blue, an AI assistant that draws upon Blancco’s accumulated data erasure history.

Articles.Title: AI alters ITAD economics

stories.Headline: AI deepfakes pose risks to consumers, voters and others, security experts warn
stories.Summary:
Advances in artificial intelligence have made it easy to create deepfake images, videos and audio recordings, and security experts told CBS News that bad actors could use them to flood people with realistic scams and spread disinformation. Deepfakes using the voices and likenesses of public figures, including celebrities and political candidates, can also deceive the public. By one measure, fewer than 10% of people can recognize an audio deepfake, according to Doppel, a social engineering defense platform. Doppel co-founder Kevin Tian said that in a test only 8% of people realized an AI agent was calling them, while 92% thought they were speaking to a human.

AI-generated advertisements featuring deepfakes of politicians have already appeared online and on social media ahead of the midterm elections. In one incident in Texas, a phony, AI-manipulated social video targeting Senate candidate James Talarico purported to show a former student accusing the Democrat of sexual misconduct, according to PolitiFact. As of mid-October, political campaigns had spent more than $137 million on at least 220 AI-generated ads, some featuring deepfakes of candidates, according to the Wesleyan Media Project. Erika Franklin Fowler, co-director of the project, said in a statement this month that it identified less than $50,000 in spending on AI-generated ads in the 2024 cycle, and she noted that in most cases the creators of the ads do not disclose that they were made using AI.

Michael Kaiser, CEO of Defending Digital Campaigns, a nonpartisan organization that provides free cybersecurity services to political campaigns, told CBS News that when people can't tell what is legitimate, they question everything. Travis Ridout, the Wesleyan project's co-director, told CBS News that even when someone suspects an ad is AI-generated or features a deepfake, the visuals can still make an impression and shape opinion, and that it sticks in one's mind. Raul Liive, a deepfake expert at the identity verification company Veriff, told CBS News that generating deepfake data gets easier every day, and that where faking someone's face once took effort and Photoshop, now a person can just prompt an AI tool. Veriff has documented a 300% increase in deepfake-related fraud attempts against businesses this year compared with 2025.

Veriff research found that consumers struggle to spot deepfakes. In one test the firm conducted, 70% of people misidentified a deepfake video of a female character as real. The old telltale signs of a deepfake, like six fingers or three hands, are also disappearing, and Veriff found that people look for unreliable visual cues such as unnatural skin or oddities in hair or teeth that AI is increasingly eliminating. Kaiser pointed to an authentic photo of Sen. Mitch McConnell posing with his wife from his hospital bed, released amid speculation that the senator had died following a medical emergency earlier this year, which some internet users suggested had been manipulated. He said people don't know if what they are looking at is legitimate or if requests for donations are real, and that questioning everything erodes trust in the whole system.

Articles.Title: AI deepfakes pose risks to consumers, voters and others, security experts warn

stories.Headline: Block Puts AI to Work Taking Orders and Preparing Purchases
stories.Summary:
Block is putting artificial intelligence to work on both sides of a sale, with voice ordering for Square customers and software that prepares purchase orders for sellers. The company announced the tools as part of its third-quarter results, which it released after markets closed on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. The new Square Kiosk lets diners ask questions about the menu and order by voice. On the business side, a product called Squaremates already prepares purchase orders for food and beverage sellers, and Block plans to add procurement agents that help manage inventory and order from suppliers.

The results came with several numbers. Square processed $76.4 billion in the third quarter, up 14% year over year, with food and beverage leading the major seller categories, retail volume up 13% and services up 8%. Cash App reached 60 million monthly transacting users in September, up 4% year over year, and its consumer loan originations rose 40% to $19 billion. Primary banking users rose to 9.4 million from 8.3 million a year earlier, and about 28 million customers used the Cash App Card monthly. Third-quarter net revenue rose to $6.7 billion from $6.1 billion a year earlier, and shares were up 6.8% in after-hours trading.

Chief Executive Jack Dorsey said during the earnings call that smaller sellers want something really easy to use and immediately accessible, and that Square can deliver that. He said sellers typically start by asking questions about their data before handing tasks to agents, and he sees a market for the AI tools beyond Square sellers, from the smallest businesses up to Block's own size and beyond. Chief Financial Officer Amrita Ahuja said new sellers joining through independent sales organizations increased 90% from the previous quarter, from a still-small share of Square's business. Block Business Lead Owen Jennings pointed to teens and families and to Neighborhoods, which connects Cash App users with participating Square sellers, and said those customers skewed toward higher household incomes than Cash App's core base.

Block enabled Neighborhoods for about 30,000 sellers in late August, and by September participating sellers represented about $5 billion in annualized gross payment volume, nearly five times the June level. Jennings said Block funds the sign-up bonuses and ongoing rewards and sets the rates for both, and he sees room for sellers to help fund rewards as they gain more customers to market to directly. Cash App moved its Borrow product primarily from four weeks with a 5% fee to six weeks with a 7.5% fee. Block is testing how to charge for the AI tools it is making available to other companies through Builder Lab and Buzz.

Articles.Title: Block Puts AI to Work Taking Orders and Preparing Purchases

stories.Headline: Jus Mundi Adds AI-Powered Arbitrator Search to Jus AI
stories.Summary:
Jus Mundi announced on Oct. 29 that it is expanding its Jus AI platform with AI-powered arbitrator search and due diligence capabilities. The new capability is designed to help arbitration lawyers identify potential arbitrators and conduct deeper research on shortlisted candidates. Jus Mundi is privately testing the new arbitrator search and due diligence capabilities within its Jus AI platform. The company is taking its arbitration-focused artificial intelligence into a new area, with a private beta aimed at helping lawyers make one of the key decisions in an arbitration case, which is who should serve as arbitrator.

Users will be able to search for candidates using criteria including language, industry and institutional experience, before using the platform for deeper research on shortlisted arbitrators. The expansion brings together Jus Mundi's legal research technology with the professional data held within Jus Connect. The company expects the beta to run for approximately three months, with a wider launch targeted for early next year. The articles do not name who at Jus Mundi is responsible for the new capability or give any statement from the company beyond the announcement details.

The articles do not say what happens next beyond the expected beta period and the targeted wider launch in early next year. They also do not give further context on how the capability will be received or used once it is more widely available. No additional details on the private beta or its participants are provided in the articles. More to follow.

stories.Headline: CERT-In Gets Mythos AI Access: Cautious Use for Cybersecurity
stories.Summary:
India's cybersecurity agency CERT-In has gained access to Anthropic's Mythos AI model, IT Ministry sources said on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The agency will begin using and experimenting with the model's capabilities. Mythos is currently available only to a small group of trusted organisations. Access is expected to help CERT-In identify cyber vulnerabilities and strengthen its response to emerging cyber threats. CERT-In will adopt a cautious and calibrated approach, with the focus first on understanding the model's capabilities, potential applications and associated risks.

The sources said the process will be slow and that anything the agency wants to test will be routed gradually. They said the whole idea is that the cure should not be worse than the problem. Wider usage will be considered only after this initial assessment. The sources said sector-specific AI norms are fine because AI's impact varies by sector, and risks are significantly larger in some critical infrastructure sectors. They backed regulators like TRAI to take the lead on sectoral guidelines.

TRAI last week proposed a draft framework for responsible AI use in telecom networks, requiring service providers to adopt board-approved AI policies, set up governance and safety committees, and report serious AI-related incidents. The IT Ministry is also preparing a consultation paper on AI regulations covering AI safety, deepfakes and a human-first approach. The sources said a uniformly tight framework would affect everyone, while rules can be somewhat tighter in difficult sectors. They said the IT Ministry works closely with regulators of critical infrastructure sectors. The development comes amid growing concerns that the same AI capabilities that help find vulnerabilities could be exploited by malicious actors for sophisticated cyberattacks.

Articles.Title: CERT-In Gets Mythos AI Access: Cautious Use for Cybersecurity

stories.Headline: TRAI proposes responsible use of AI in telecom networks, to make telcos accountable
stories.Summary:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India released a draft framework on Friday for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in telecom networks. The draft, issued for stakeholder consultation, would require service providers to adopt board-approved AI policies, set up dedicated governance and safety committees, and report serious AI-related incidents to the regulator. It also seeks to hold entities accountable for the outcomes of AI systems in their networks and services, whether those systems are built internally, bought from a third party, or a mix of both. TRAI said it floated the draft titled Guidelines on Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services for stakeholders' comments.

Under the proposals, operators and other authorised entities using AI must sort their systems into high, medium and low-risk categories based on their importance to network operations, financial and operational results, and possible effects on consumers. Each entity must have an internal AI policy approved by its board or equivalent body, covering risk classification, deployment approvals, incident management, human oversight, data governance and consumer grievance redressal. AI incidents would be classed as critical, high, moderate or low severity, and critical and high-severity incidents must be reported to TRAI in a set format and timeframe. Companies would also keep central databases of AI incidents and consumer complaints involving AI-related harm, and all AI systems would need appropriate human oversight.

The draft requires an AI Governance and Safety Committee, led by a senior executive designated as the AI Governance and Safety Officer, to oversee deployment and spot vulnerabilities, fairness concerns and emerging systemic risks. The committee would review deployed systems at least once every financial year and ensure corrective steps, including modifying or decommissioning systems where needed. Operators would need validation, conformity and impact assessments before deploying new AI systems or changing existing ones, covering accuracy, robustness, explainability, fairness, resilience against model drift and human oversight. They would also keep an up-to-date inventory of all active, inactive and decommissioned AI systems, and no AI system could be used unless it is in the inventory.

TRAI said AI is increasingly being integrated into telecom networks and services, and the guidelines aim to ensure consistent and responsible implementation of the India AI Governance Guidelines in the sector and to increase clarity, predictability and accountability. It noted that growing AI use could improve efficiency but also bring risks from unintended model behaviour, biases and adversarial attacks that could affect critical infrastructure resilience. The rules would apply to any entity holding a licence under the Telegraph Act, 1885, or an authorisation under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, that uses or intends to use AI systems in telecom networks or services. Stakeholder comments on the draft are invited by November 27.

Articles.Title: TRAI proposes new AI guidelines for telecom networks

stories.Headline: Northstar Security launches with $7M to detect toxic risk combinations
stories.Summary:
Northstar Security came out of stealth mode with $7 million in seed funding, the company announced on November 2, 2026. Wing Venture Capital led the round, with participation from MVP, Outliers, and cybersecurity veterans Gerhard Eschelbeck, Renaud Deraison, and Justin Somaini. The startup builds AI agents that find "toxic combinations" of security risks, where issues that are manageable on their own together expose critical business systems. One example the company gives is a laptop without endpoint protection whose owner has privileged access to a critical payroll system.

The platform pulls data from more than 70 enterprise security and IT products, including Okta, GitHub, Workday, Microsoft Defender and Entra, AWS, and Google Cloud. It builds a real-time Security Context Graph showing connections among identities, assets, applications, vulnerabilities, and business systems. Analysts can investigate findings using plain language queries, and the agents can start fixes such as installing endpoint protection or limiting access, with human oversight. Customers can also connect external AI agents to the graph through the Model Context Protocol to build custom security workflows.

Amer Deeba, the CEO and co-founder, said security teams are overwhelmed with data but lack context. Deeba previously co-founded Normalyze, which Proofpoint acquired, and was a senior executive at Qualys. Ed Rowe, co-founder and CTO, was formerly CTO at Farmers Business Network and SVP of engineering at AppDynamics. The company said the new funding will support platform development, hiring, and expansion of go-to-market efforts.

Articles.Title: Northstar Security launches with $7M to detect toxic risk combinations

stories.Headline: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for AI Agent Management Platforms
stories.Summary:
Microsoft was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI Agent Management Platforms, according to a Microsoft Security Blog post published on November 3, 2026. The post was written by Nadim Abdo and Ray Smith. The Gartner report is dated October 27, 2026, and its authors listed are Andrei Razvan Sachelarescu, Lucas Kobat, Gilbert van der Heiden and Max Goss. Microsoft credits the recognition to its approach to helping organizations manage, secure and scale AI investments through Microsoft Agent 365.

More than 50 million agents have been registered in Agent 365 since its introduction, the post says. Microsoft says its approach starts with identity rather than monitoring: Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives every agent a unique ID tied to an owner and purpose, with access controls that adjust as risk signals change. Agent 365 extends tools IT and security teams already use, including Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Intune and the Microsoft 365 admin center. It supports agents from Microsoft, customer-built agents, local agents on devices and partner clouds, with current integrations including Agentforce, Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, Databricks, Google Gemini and Google Vertex, and planned integrations including OpenAI, ServiceNow and Snowflake.

Microsoft says it is expanding discovery to 35 additional local agent types, bringing the total to 60, and adding support to discover unknown agents. It is also extending policy coverage and controls to managed and unmanaged agents, including third-party agents. The new Agent 365 Action Center is described as helping IT and security leaders move from reactive alerts to prescriptive actions, such as cleaning up inactive agents, reassigning ownerless agents or automatically blocking agents based on risk. Microsoft says it is also advancing cost management, task classification and value calculation.

Agent 365 is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on to Microsoft 365 E5, the post says. Microsoft says it is previewing discovery of cloud agents and plans more integrations soon. The post says Microsoft is attending Microsoft Ignite 2026, held November 17 to 20, 2026, where it will share more about what is next for Agent 365. Gartner's disclaimer states that it does not endorse any vendor, product or service in its publications and that its publications consist of the opinions of its research organization.

Microsoft reported quarterly revenue of $92.29 billion on October 28, an increase of 18.8% that beat market expectations, according to Barchart. Operating income rose 21% to $45.9 billion, and GAAP earnings per share rose 32% to $4.92. Excluding the impact of its OpenAI investments, earnings per share rose 18% to $4.89. Azure revenue climbed to $33.2 billion from $22.4 billion a year earlier, and Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9 billion. Commercial remaining performance obligations rose 73% to $677 billion, and Microsoft said roughly 30% of that is expected to be recognized over the next 12 months.

Capital expenditures reached $45.2 billion in the first quarter, and management said on its earnings call that spending should top $50 billion in the second quarter and total approximately $170 billion for calendar year 2026. About three-quarters of first-quarter capital expenditures went toward shorter-lived assets, mainly CPUs and GPUs, along with higher memory and storage costs. Cash flow from operations reached $58 billion, up 29% year-over-year, while free cash flow came in at $18.6 billion. Microsoft expects Azure revenue growth of 49% to 50% in constant currency for the second quarter, with demand continuing to exceed available supply, according to MorningStar. stories.Headline: flipkart appoints hemant badri to lead ai transformation charter
stories.Summary:
Flipkart has appointed Hemant Badri to lead its AI transformation charter, the company announced in April 2026. CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy announced the move, which signals a push to make Flipkart an AI-first organisation. Badri currently serves as SVP and Head of Supply Chain, Customer Experience and Re-Commerce. He will take on the new responsibility in addition to his existing roles.

The charter calls for embedding intelligent systems into Flipkart's core operations. Badri will focus on identifying and operationalising business use cases where AI can have the biggest impact. He will work closely with Balaji Thiagarajan, who continues to lead technology strategy for an AI-native Flipkart. The AI-first vision covers a more intuitive customer experience, more efficient seller tools and higher internal productivity through automating routine tasks.

Krishnamurthy said the approach means intelligent systems will sit at the core of Flipkart's development. He stressed a human-in-the-loop approach, saying technology should sharpen rather than replace intuition built over years. He said AI solutions should stay grounded in the needs of customers and sellers. The shift will require ownership across all functions and teams at Flipkart.

Badri's operational depth is expected to help make AI a practical reality across the organisation. For developers and tech leaders, the articles say the move signals a need to align work with AI-native principles. They also point to new opportunities for AI application within e-commerce workflows. Flipkart is owned by Walmart.

stories.Headline: stop doing repetitive work start building tiny systems
stories.Summary:
The TechGig article, published on February 20, 2026, describes developers automating their personal workflows with small tools. It says developers are using AutoHotKey for keyboard shortcuts that expand short triggers into full text. It says they are running encrypted, scheduled backups through Zerobyte on top of Restic, and building AI-powered workflows in n8n for Gmail and expense logging. It also says they are writing small Python scripts for recurring routines.

The article says AutoHotKey shortcuts work system-wide after a small script file is run once. It says Zerobyte runs in Docker, mounts local folders as volumes, defines repository targets, sets schedules and retention policies, and prunes old backups automatically, with data encrypted before it leaves the machine. It says n8n can capture a short Telegram message about spending, have an AI parser extract the amount, category and date, and send the data to Google Sheets. It says n8n can also monitor Gmail and auto-label emails using AI classification, with thread history fetched from the inbox and sent folder to give context. It says a single script replacing a 10-minute task done five times a week saves over 40 hours a year.

The article says senior engineers understand rule-based automation in production systems but rarely apply it to their own workflows. It says the real problem is cognitive load rather than time, calling repeated typing, backup checks and inbox scrolling a mental drag and an attention tax. It advises starting small by identifying one repetitive task done three times last week and asking whether it is rule-based. It says not to automate everything at once and to ship one tiny system per week. It adds that open-source tools like n8n, Restic and Docker suit cost-conscious, self-hosted setups, with no subscriptions and no black-box SaaS dependency.

Articles.Title: stop doing repetitive work start building tiny systems

stories.Headline: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 2, 2026 that it is raising rewards in its Security Bug Bounty program. The company said the change is meant to encourage independent researchers to look for vulnerabilities in OpenAI software that its own testing may have missed. OpenAI also said it is adding new incentives so researchers can earn more for higher quality vulnerability reports. The announcement was published on OpenAI's website.

OpenAI said it is more than quadrupling the midpoint of its reward ranges for medium, high, and critical findings on average. A critical vulnerability in a core product such as ChatGPT, Codex, or the API Platform will now earn up to $30,000. Exceptional critical findings on those targets remain eligible for up to $100,000, and now up to $172,000 with bonuses. The program also adds a quality bonus multiplier, a 5-tier loyalty bonus program, and priority campaign multipliers with dedicated bonus pools for newly launched features.

OpenAI said independent security researchers play an essential role in protecting technology across the industry. It said incentivizing responsible disclosure is a core part of its security model and complements its Defense Factory work, where engineers use its models to find weaknesses, reproduce them, and test fixes. The company said the updates are designed to encourage and empower researchers and to build a collaborative, community-first security environment. OpenAI thanked everyone who has investigated a lead and reported it.

For reports already submitted but not yet awarded a bounty, OpenAI said it will apply the new reward ranges. For bounties awarded in the 30 days before the announcement, it will pay the difference if the finding would have earned more under the new ranges, based on the base award plus loyalty awards. OpenAI's security team will be at PROMPT2PWN in Oakland on November 20, 21, where researchers can test targets in person. The company said it wants OpenAI to be a team researchers come back to when they find something it has missed.

Articles.Title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties

stories.Headline: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
stories.Summary:
OpenAI said on November 2, 2026 that it is planning its next internal security sprint, which will bring new researchers and security partners together with its own teams to test and strengthen its systems using its models. The company is partnering with Cathedral, whose researchers will use OpenAI's models alongside OpenAI teams to challenge its defenses and look for weaknesses. OpenAI is also making changes to its Security Bug Bounty program, including more than quadrupling rewards for critical findings. The work builds on OpenAI's last sprint, in which 25 percent of its product engineers were dedicated to finding and fixing weaknesses. Using Codex, those engineers investigated findings, reproduced vulnerabilities in isolated environments and prepared patches for review.

OpenAI said traditional cyber defenses alone are no longer sufficient, pointing to recent incidents across the industry. It has committed $1 billion in subsidized access over six months for frontline defenders protecting essential services and digital infrastructure. Gavin Kliger, CEO and co-founder of Cathedral, said OpenAI is setting an important example by partnering with outside security firms and using its own models to continuously test and strengthen its defenses. He said every company should be thinking about how to put these capabilities to work. He said Cathedral is excited to collaborate with OpenAI's teams, combining their models and security expertise with Cathedral's research to find weaknesses, test fixes and strengthen this approach to continuous defense.

OpenAI said the effort is part of its ongoing work to use AI to continuously find and fix weaknesses in its systems. It is sharing its architecture and lessons from the last sprint, along with its blueprint for empowering cyber defenders across industry and government. OpenAI said it will keep advancing its models, using them to strengthen its own systems and expanding access for trusted defenders. It said keeping the defender's window open will take action across the industry and that the work needs to start now.

Articles.Title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI

stories.Headline: AMD Reports Tuesday as Ex-Stability AI CEO Warns “There Are Not Enough CPUs in the World”
stories.Summary:
Advanced Micro Devices reports third-quarter results after the close on Tuesday, days after Intel sank 28% on a fourth-quarter outlook hurt by weak PC demand and too few server chips to sell. On Saturday's episode of the Moonshots podcast, former Stability AI CEO Emad Mostaque said that at 10 AI agents per American, there would not be enough CPUs in the world, and that the CPU build-out, with a two to three year lag, is only just starting. Intel's data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion in the third quarter, but shortages of wafers and substrates limit how much it can ship. AMD guided third-quarter revenue to about $13.0 billion, plus or minus $300 million, and analysts expect $13.09 billion.

AMD's management put the 2030 server CPU market at about $60 billion at its November 2025 analyst day and raised that to about $220 billion on its August earnings call. In the second quarter, its server CPU sales to cloud customers and to enterprise customers each grew more than 70% from a year earlier, and its server share was already about 40% at the 2025 analyst day, with a goal of more than 50%. Analysts expect AMD's revenue to more than triple, from $34.6 billion in 2025 to $125 billion in 2028. AMD still gets about 27% of its sales from PCs, and management expects higher memory and component prices to weigh on PC and gaming demand in the second half.

Mostaque said the market is missing something huge, and he thinks the GPU build-out is already well underway, including AMD's own MI450, but agents need CPUs to carry out their tasks. Kunjan Sobhani, senior semiconductor analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said the only good news is that Intel's server CPU demand continues to stay strong, while shortages of wafers and substrates limit shipments. Intel guides fourth-quarter revenue to $15.0 to $16.0 billion, below the third quarter's $16.5 billion, and expects client revenue to fall more than 20% from the third quarter. New Street Research upgraded Intel on Oct. 26, arguing that server CPU supply will stay tight for years.

AMD is short on server chips too, and management expects its supply to improve in 2027. Management says server CPUs carry gross margins above the company average, and AMD's operating margin rose from 10.6% in the quarter to Sept. 28, 2024, to 17.3% in the quarter to June 27, 2026, with the exception of a loss in the June 2025 quarter when about $800 million of MI308 charges hit. The hyperscalers design their own server CPUs on designs from Arm Holdings, and AMD says its Venice chips deliver up to 3.3x the performance per watt of leading Arm chips. Another panelist on the same show argued that stronger models may need fewer agents, which would mean fewer CPUs, and the build-out Mostaque describes takes two to three years, so one quarter will not show whether he is right.

stories.Headline: a16z generative ai - The Chimes
stories.Summary:
Story, the global intellectual property blockchain, announced an integration with Stability AI’s models to support open-source AI development. The collaboration is meant to let creators, developers and artists capture value from their contributions by using blockchain to track attribution and monetization of works generated through AI. Story said creators could register unique styles or voices as intellectual property with transparent usage terms, so others could train and fine-tune AI models on that IP and all contributors in the creative chain would benefit when outputs are monetized. Scott Trowbridge, Vice President of Stability AI, said the company was thrilled to see its models used in Story’s blockchain technology to ensure proper attribution and reward contributors. PIP Labs, an initial core contributor to the Story Network, is backed by investors including a16z crypto, Endeavor and Polychain.

Separately, the healthcare AI startup Hippocratic AI Inc. said it closed a $141 million Series B funding round, bringing its total raised to more than $278 million. Chief Executive Officer Munjal Shah said the last nine months since the company’s previous $50 million round had seen it receive its first U.S. patents, fully evaluate and verify the safety of its first AI healthcare agents, and sign contracts with 23 health systems, payers and pharma clients. He said the round would accelerate development and deployment of the company’s generative AI-driven super staffing and continue its quest to make healthcare abundance a reality. The startup, co-founded by Shah and a group of physicians, hospital administrators, healthcare professionals and AI researchers, said clinicians can create an AI agent prototype in their area of focus in less than 30 minutes, and around three to four hours to develop one that can be tested.

Hippocratic AI said it only works with licensed clinicians to develop its agents and verifies their qualifications and experience first. Once clinicians build an agent, it is submitted to the startup for an initial round of testing, followed by more extensive evaluations and safety assessments by a network of more than 6,000 nurses and 300 doctors who confirm it passes all required safety tests. Clinicians who created an agent will be able to claim a share of the revenue it generates from the startup’s customers, and each will have a dashboard to track performance and receive feedback. The startup said its agent creators include Dr. Vanessa Dorismond, an obstetrician and gynecologist at El Camino Women’s Medical Group and Teal Health, who helped create an agent focused on cervical cancer check-ins and patient education, and Kristina Dulaney, RN, PMH-C, founder of Cherished Mom, who helped create an agent for postpartum mental health assessments and depression screening. Its early customers include Arkos Health, Belong Health, Cincinnati Children’s, Fraser Health Authority in Canada, GuideHealth, Honor Health, Deca Dental Management, OhioHealth and WellSpan Health.

Andreessen Horowitz, or a16z, led a $24 million Series A round in Raspberry AI, the generative AI platform for fashion creatives, with existing investors Greycroft, Correlation Ventures and MVP Ventures joining along with angel investors including Gokul Rajaram and Ken Pilot. Raspberry AI said the funding would accelerate product development and add engineering, sales and marketing talent, and its technology is being used by Under Armour, MCM Worldwide, Gruppo Teddy and Li & Fung to create and iterate apparel, footwear and accessories styles. The same day, a16z also led a Series A investment in Slingshot AI, which has raised a total of $40 million to create a foundation model for psychology. a16z participated in a round that funded Anysphere on January 14, 2025, with a total of $105 million for an AI coding tool known as Cursor, whose valuation has reached $2.5 billion, and it has released a $500 million Biotech Ecosystem Venture Fund with Eli Lilly focused on health technologies.

stories.Headline: India floats AI plan under which ‘The model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model’
stories.Summary:
India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has floated a plan to regulate how AI models are trained on local data. The scheme is called the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture for AI Training, or DEPA. Professor Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, described it as a setup where the model travels to the data rather than the data travelling to the model. The motive is to create AI models trained on local data, because the government thinks offshore model-makers won’t be motivated to address the nation’s issues or to ensure data owners stay in control.

Under the plan, Training Data Providers such as hospitals, banks and government agencies would share anonymized and encrypted data with a Data Exchange Platform. Entities called Training Data Consumers would access that data to train their models. The platforms would run hardware-based Secure Data Environments in which data remains encrypted and isolated even during processing, and they would enforce rules set by the data providers on how consumers can use the data. The framework says differential privacy techniques would be applied to prevent a model from learning or revealing individual specific information, and all activity inside the secure environments would be immutably logged for audit purposes.

MeitY’s framework says DEPA could unlock fragmented health data for AI-driven diagnostics, drug discovery and public health management. It says the scheme could enable secure sharing of financial data and potentially extend formal credit to 400 million underserved individuals and MSMEs. In education, it says DEPA could enable AI-powered personalized learning for millions and create portable skill credentials for the nation’s 250 million students in a $29 billion EdTech sector. The framework also presents DEPA as India’s contribution to global science diplomacy, advancing efforts by institutions such as the World Bank and the United Nations to shape a more inclusive and responsible global AI ecosystem.

India’s government already operates several data exchanges, but the article says it is unclear how much work remains to make DEPA a reality. The framework makes several mentions of digital public infrastructure, an idea pioneered by India in which the government funds tools like the Unified Payments Interface payment system and the Bharat Taxi zero-commission ride-sharing platform. India also uses its digital public infrastructure as a diplomatic tool by giving it away to friendly nations. The article does not say what happens next beyond the framework’s stated goals.

Articles.Title: India floats AI plan under which ‘The model travels to the data, rather than the data travelling to the model’

stories.Headline: Zyphra AI Introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA): A Path to True Subquadratic Attention
stories.Summary:
Zyphra AI released Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), a sparse attention method built around a tree-structured indexer, in a technical paper posted on November 3, 2026. The method targets a known gap in sparse attention, where the indexer that picks tokens still scans the whole context. Zyphra says ZHA can be distilled into frozen pretrained models with about 4 billion tokens. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B it stays close to dense attention on reasoning, agentic coding and 256K retrieval benchmarks.

ZHA adds 81,920 trainable parameters to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, about 0.00024%, and was tested up to 256K context. It retrofits frozen pretrained models after a 4 billion token KL warmup at 32K context, and its speedups come from a modeled H100 BF16 roofline, with no optimized kernels released. An FP4 router variant was also tested. The team converted Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with two trees, a deep one with chunk size 4 and 6 levels and a wide one with chunk size 256 and 1 level, both using 16 reference queries and p = 0.95. It also trained a MiniMax Sparse Attention indexer on 40 billion tokens, 10 times ZHA's budget.

On the benchmarks, the deep tree scored 63.4% on LongBench v2 against 58.0% for dense attention, using about 1.1% of keys. The worst result was on NoPE-based Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B, where deep-tree RULER-13 dropped 25.3 points below dense. MSA fell to 77.1% on RULER-13 while both ZHA trees stayed above 93%. Across 28 tree geometries, RULER accuracy held steady when attending to 10 to 30% of keys, and a 4-parameter model predicts RULER accuracy from geometry with 1.44-point RMSE. All numbers were self-reported by Zyphra, and the paper is on arXiv as 2610.42112.

Articles.Title: Zyphra AI Introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA): A Path to True Subquadratic Attention

stories.Headline: The Letter Company Releases Letterpress-1: A Coding Agent Built for Growth Engineering
stories.Summary:
The Letter Company released the beta of Letterpress-1 on November 3, 2026, according to MarkTechPost. It is a coding agent, harness and IDE built for growth engineering. The agent reads a website and its market, then decides what should exist. It builds the change in a sandbox and opens a pull request with a live preview.

The agent is aimed at teams that host their marketing site in git, and it suggests the next thing to build. Examples include de-anonymization, landing pages, warmed emails, blog automation and agent telemetry. Every change follows the same loop: the agent reads the site, plans and builds in a sandbox, reviews its own change, then opens a pull request. Nothing lands until the user chooses a preview, a pull request, or a merge after checks pass. The team lists six surfaces, including a web platform, a Slack app, a CLI and a website portal.

The Letter team says the agent combines frontier models with fine-tuned small models, though names and sizes are not disclosed. It runs on Letter's hosted platform against a git repository, needs no local GPU, and setup takes under five minutes, per Letter. There is no public benchmark, and Letter shows one self-reported, side-by-side page build against Codex. The entry plan is $100 per month with overage at five times the list rate. The team argues that websites, unlike apps, react to outside forces such as agent behavior, Google rankings, human visits and competitor activity.

The launch post highlights four primitives: Proofs, Simulations, Benches and Phantoms. Proofs are signed evidence of customer success built from telemetry and billing data for agent visitors. Simulations are mirror versions of an API or MCP with simulated data so agents can try before buying. Benches are self-hosted, reproducible benchmark apps with open-source code and independent governance, and Phantoms are independent, autonomous blogs used to sandbox growth strategies. The site adds Kernels, Letterbases, Visitors and Mailers, and it watches competitor sitemaps to flag new pages.

Articles.Title: The Letter Company Releases Letterpress-1: A Coding Agent Built for Growth Engineering

stories.Headline: Deep Principle Releases Hydrogen-1.0: A 753B Open-Weight Model for Scientific Discovery
stories.Summary:
Deep Principle released Hydrogen-1.0 on November 2, 2026, according to MarkTechPost. It is an open-weight scientific model for chemistry, materials science and life sciences. The company built it by post-training Z.ai's GLM-5.3 on domain data, laboratory records and agent discovery trajectories. The weights ship under the MIT License.

The model has 753 billion parameters in a mixture-of-experts design, with about 40 billion active, a 1M-token context and 128K maximum output. It runs on 8 GPUs with SGLang in testing, using NVFP4 for NVIDIA B200 and B300 and MXFP4 for AMD MI350X and MI355X. Deep Principle reports 38.3% on FrontierScience-Research against 33.3% for GPT-6-Astra, a self-reported result. It trails GPT-6-Astra by 3.33 points on NMR structure elucidation, and a founder's thread reports 93.0% on GPQA-Diamond, roughly matching Kimi-K3. Full datasets and recipes are not released.

Deep Principle is a Hangzhou-based AI-for-materials company, and its model card describes Hydrogen-1.0 as a GLM-5.3 derivative for scientific problem solving. The team says proprietary models produced recent AI science results but their discovery capabilities are not open, so Hydrogen-1.0 is its attempt at a reproducible, inspectable alternative. The pipeline combines supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning, drawing on domain knowledge, research scenarios, laboratory records captured through Mira and discovery trajectories that include failed attempts. The technical post shows four demos, including building a polyethylene melt in GROMACS, growing an Ireland-Claisen reaction network of 27 structures and writing a JSON protocol for a 12-vial Suzuki coupling study.

On scientific computing Hydrogen-1.0 leads by 5.13 percentage points, and on forward reaction prediction it leads by 4.76 points. In transition metal complex design over 5 rounds, it reached a mean best-so-far HOMO-LUMO gap of 4.318 eV, against 3.689 eV for GPT-6-Astra and 3.353 eV for Kimi-K3. On 117 experiment-planning questions it scored above Kimi-K3, while GPT-6-Astra and Opus-5.5 were excluded after refusing more than 50% of requests. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: Deep Principle Releases Hydrogen-1.0: A 753B Open-Weight Model for Scientific Discovery

stories.Headline: NVIDIA Releases Auto Ontology: An Open Semantic Layer That Grounds AI Agent SQL
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA released Auto Ontology on November 2, 2026, according to MarkTechPost. It is an open library under the Apache 2.0 license that builds a context layer from enterprise metadata. Agents use that layer to write SQL against certified business definitions. The repository says a fast revenue answer is worthless if the number is wrong.

The library uses nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b as its default model, with Nemotron embedding and reranking models. It runs on Docker Compose for a local stack or Kubernetes via Helm, and inference uses hosted NVIDIA NIM endpoints or self-hosted NIMs. The stack has four core services: a Next.js 16 frontend on port 3000, a FastAPI backend with LangChain on port 3001, an ingestion worker on port 3002, and Postgres with pgvector for the catalog, ontology and vectors. Source databases can be Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake or DuckDB, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works.

The MCP server docs describe nine read-only tools, and ask_question returns the answer, the SQL and the rows as separate fields, with results capped at 100 rows. There is no tool for browsing raw schemas, which NVIDIA chose on purpose so agents reach data through the semantic layer. The OpenAPI spec publishes 87 operations, sign-in runs through OAuth, and every call carries the signed-in user's permissions. NVIDIA's developer page frames the output as a starting ontology that business experts still test, refine and certify.

NVIDIA reports that ontology creation time was cut by 90% in its own testing, but no text-to-SQL accuracy scores have been published. The separate auto-ontology-eval harness runs two arms in NeMo Gym, a schema-only LLM control and the ontology-grounded agent, with scoring by deterministic execution match and no LLM judge. Bundled datasets include BIRD Dev with 1,534 questions across 11 databases, Mini-Dev with 500 questions, FDABench-Lite with 169 questions, and BEAVER with a default 100-question sample. The harness repo notes two limitations: optional few-shot exemplars and value anchors go to the ontology arm only, and its tested configuration routes both arms through a Claude model on NVIDIA's inference gateway.

Articles.Title: NVIDIA Releases Auto Ontology: An Open Semantic Layer That Grounds AI Agent SQL

stories.Headline: Meet qwenGPU: Qwen3.5-2B With 45 Compiled GPU Layers That Run CUDA
stories.Summary:
qwenGPU is an experimental model that compiles a SIMT GPU directly into the weights of Qwen3.5-2B. Developer Vixhal released it on GitHub under the MIT license. The model runs real CUDA, compiled to NVIDIA PTX, inside its own forward passes. It tests one idea for developers, exact computation inside a pretrained LLM rather than beside it.

The model combines Qwen3.5-2B, which has 24 layers, with 45 compiled GPU layers, for 69 in total. It keeps the base model's context of 262,144 tokens. It runs on Apple silicon, an NVIDIA GPU or a CPU, with about 16 GB of free memory, and there is no quantized build. The GPU is a 4-lane SIMT machine with 15 registers per lane, a 4-stage pipeline, a 32-block ROM and 126 memory words.

The developer reports that every launch in his runs was exact, with text drift at a KL of about 7e-4. The reference interpreter matched a real NVIDIA Tesla T4 on 49 of 49 kernels. Speed was about 10 to 15 tokens per second on Apple MPS, and Qwen-written CUDA passed 4 of 5 tests. The README warns that a 2B model's CUDA is still unreliable.

The circuit is muted on text tokens and Qwen's own weights are unchanged, so the merged model's next-token distribution stays close to the original. In normal mode, Qwen writes an expression for ready-made kernels, and it answered 20 of 24 sampled chat questions with GPU-computed numbers. In advanced mode, Qwen writes the CUDA kernel itself and was correct first try on 4 of 5 questions. qwenGPU uses the transformer compiler from Qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal, which compiles a 32-bit RISC-V CPU into Qwen3.5-4B.

Articles.Title: Meet qwenGPU: Qwen3.5-2B With 45 Compiled GPU Layers That Run CUDA

stories.Headline: Lovable backer Creandum raises $750m for largest-ever fund to back AI boom
stories.Summary:
Creandum, the venture capital firm that backed Lovable, raised $750m for its largest-ever fund to invest in artificial intelligence, Sifted reported on 2 November 2026. The firm said the new fund is its biggest to date and is aimed at backing the AI boom. Creandum is known as a backer of Lovable, the AI coding startup. The report did not give further details of the fund's size beyond the $750m figure.

The fund is intended to back companies in the AI boom, according to the report. It is the largest fund Creandum has raised. The articles did not say how many investors contributed or what specific sectors the money will target. They also did not give a timetable for when the fund will be deployed.

Creandum is responsible for the fund, and the report attributes the $750m figure to the firm. The articles did not include direct statements from Creandum executives beyond the fund's purpose of backing AI. No named person was quoted in the material provided. stories.Headline: Enterprise customers want to see AI’s ROI. Here’s how startups can show it
stories.Summary:
Enterprise customers want to see a return on their investment in AI, according to Sifted. The article is a guide for startups on how to show that return. It was published on 2 November 2026. The article gives advice rather than reporting a single event.

The article says startups should show enterprise customers the value of AI in clear terms. It focuses on how startups can demonstrate return on investment to these customers. The piece is aimed at founders selling AI to large companies. It does not give specific figures or name individual companies.

The responsibility for proving the return falls on the startups selling AI, the article suggests. It frames the issue around what enterprise customers want to see. The guidance is directed at how startups can meet that demand. No named people are quoted in the text provided.
