SK hynix said at its call on Wednesday that it had signed such agreements with 14 customers, including major cloud computing companies.

SK hynix's contracts typically run for five years, with extensions under discussion with some customers, and the company has already secured buyers for more than half of its total production capacity for 2027 and 2028. Including deals still under negotiation, its DRAM and high bandwidth memory output is effectively sold out through 2029. Samsung said it aims to allocate 60 to 70 percent of its total production capacity to long-term contracts by 2030, and that talks to extend agreements with some customers were in their final stages, with requested volumes far exceeding expectations. SK hynix said the contracts reflect market price fluctuations within a price range agreed with customers, and it plans to use them to secure stable revenue while allocating remaining capacity according to market conditions.

Samsung said the expansion of long-term agreements would greatly help establish a stable, contract-based business model, and that it had received requests for additional supplies during existing contract periods and was reviewing its medium-to-long-term production capabilities. SK hynix said it plans to accelerate construction of main structures at its Yongin facility in Gyeonggi and its M17 plant in Cheongju, North Chungcheong, while opening clean rooms in phases. Samsung said overall capital spending is expected to increase significantly in 2027 on the back of strong earnings in 2026, but various factors are likely to prevent that investment from translating into higher bit output in 2028. Park Jun-young, an analyst at Hanwha Investment & Securities, said that unlike in the past, higher investment no longer directly translates to higher output, which could keep memory prices rising for longer than expected.

The market remains concerned about a potential supply glut in the coming years, as major technology companies face mounting costs from AI investments and Chinese chipmakers expand production capacity. New factories are expected to begin significantly increasing DRAM supplies around 2028, according to market research firms including TrendForce. Despite a record combined third quarter operating profit of 190.77 trillion won, comprising 107.44 trillion won for Samsung and 83.33 trillion won for SK hynix, the companies' shares remained well below their peaks. At Friday's close, Samsung shares were 39.9 percent below their 52-week intraday high, while SK hynix shares were 52.5 percent below theirs. Both companies plan to adjust the pace of capacity expansion to guard against a potential supply glut, with Samsung intending to secure factory space first and install equipment in line with demand.

Articles.Title: Samsung, SK hynix build long-term order pipelines on back of continued AI chip demand

stories.Headline: Seoul shares down over 2 pct late Tues. morning on AI concerns
stories.Summary:
South Korean stocks traded more than 2 percent lower late Tuesday morning, led by technology losses over concerns about the fast pace of artificial intelligence spending. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index opened 2.46 percent lower and stood at 5,714.06 as of 11:20 a.m., down 145.02 points, or 2.48 percent. Overnight on Wall Street, the Nasdaq Composite closed 1.07 percent lower and the S&P 500 fell 0.51 percent ahead of the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday. Investor sentiment was weakened by worries that heavy spending on AI infrastructure is hurting tech firms' near-term profitability.

In Seoul, technology shares led the decline. Samsung Electronics fell 2.95 percent, and chipmaker SK hynix slid 3.8 percent. Hanmi Semiconductor dropped 4.17 percent, and SK Square, the parent of SK hynix, tumbled 4 percent. Steel giant POSCO Holdings slumped 5.3 percent, and oil refiner SK Innovation plunged 7.76 percent. The Korean won was trading at 1,341 won against the U.S. dollar as of 11:20 a.m., up 3.4 won from the previous session's close.

The articles do not name any person or official as responsible or give any statements from them. They also do not say what happens next beyond the market figures reported for late Tuesday morning. The decline was attributed to concerns over the excessive pace of AI spending and to the U.S. midterm elections. No further details on future trading or official responses are given.

Articles.Title: Seoul shares down over 2 pct late Tues. morning on AI concerns

stories.Headline: MAS’ Future of Finance Institute starts operations with AI focus; names interim CEO
stories.Summary:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore launched the Future of Finance Institute on Nov 3, and it began operations that day with a focus on AI in finance. The institute was first announced in June, with the aim of speeding up the adoption of new financial technologies and encouraging innovation in the financial sector. Alan Lim, who heads the financial infrastructure and AI office at MAS, is serving as interim CEO of the FFI at the same time as his existing role. MAS said he will lead the institute’s strategy and operations as it builds out its programmes and deepens partnerships in the financial and technology ecosystems.

The FFI will bring financial institutions together to share practical experience in implementing AI, develop good practices for deploying agentic AI, and strengthen the management of risks from AI use. To start, it will work through three pillars, PathFin.ai, BuildFin.ai and SafeFin.ai. Under PathFin.ai it will build on the existing programme and widen the range of solutions available through its knowledge hub, and it will also gather industry practitioners to discuss common challenges and practical approaches to AI adoption. Under BuildFin.ai it will work with industry players on guidance, good practices, industry standards, and common tools and infrastructure for deploying AI, with a focus on the safe use of AI agents in financial services.

Under SafeFin.ai it will promote sound AI risk management practices. MAS managing director Chia Der Jiun said the FFI will seek to anchor key capabilities in Singapore and connect the ecosystem to speed up innovation and support safe adoption of new technologies. The launch comes as banks and regulators become increasingly concerned about the risks that rapid AI adoption may bring to the financial industry. MAS said the FFI will progressively expand into other areas of financial innovation, including tokenisation.

Articles.Title: MAS’ Future of Finance Institute starts operations with AI focus; names interim CEO

stories.Headline: Deoksu Palace brings imperial feasts back to life with AI exhibition
stories.Summary:
Visitors to Deoksu Palace in Seoul can use artificial intelligence to create banquet dishes inspired by the Korean Empire. The Korea Heritage Service's Deoksu Palace Management Office, working with Davero Art, will open the exhibition "Imperial Banquet of the Korean Empire, Prepared With AI" on Tuesday at Dondeokjeon Hall. It runs through March 28, 2027. The exhibition combines research into royal Western-style banquets with generative AI.

More than 60 artifacts and exhibition items related to royal banquets will be on display, including chandeliers with the imperial plum blossom emblem, iron cooking utensils and matching tableware. At the center are 30 ingredient models, including lamb, pheasant, salmon, truffles and caviar. Visitors place ingredients on a banquet table, where sensors identify them and generative AI produces images of the dishes. A large language model then creates menu names and culinary stories in Korean and English, and the experience takes about five minutes. A 27-meter LED media wall will show a recreated imperial banquet with Korean Empire officials and foreign diplomats.

The Deoksu Palace Management Office said it hopes the exhibition will help visitors understand imperial banquet culture in an accessible and engaging way. It also said the show offers a new experience of cultural heritage through digital technology. The project was developed through a public-private partnership with Davero Art, which was selected for the Korea Creative Content Agency's 2026 AI Content Production Support Program. The exhibition draws on a decade of research, reconstruction and exhibitions on the Korean Empire's royal banquet culture by the heritage agency.

Articles.Title: Deoksu Palace brings imperial feasts back to life with AI exhibition

stories.Headline: Indie studios hide their demos as AI copycats circle
stories.Summary:
Korean indie studio YNOT pulled the public demo of its upcoming restaurant management game Spookitchen, set in a spooky Halloween town, on Oct. 20 after being warned that someone planned to clone it with AI. About a month earlier, its two developers, who go by Sini Ming and Seori Ming, received two threatening emails saying the sender intended to borrow the game's mechanics and make it with AI, and telling them there was no stopping the copying, so they should not waste their time and should just share the release date and price. Sini Ming announced the closure in a thread on X on Oct. 20 and thanked users who had sent encouragement and advice. Japanese indie studio Alliance Arts canceled the public demo of its Russian roulette-style drinking game Drunken Goddess Reflux on Oct. 16, three days before it was due to go live for Steam Next Fest, and switched to closed play sessions for a limited number of participants. In September, Weasel Pit, developer of the indie game Iron Pilgrim, made public a threatening email it had received warning that a copy would go on sale first unless the developer handed over $200 worth of Steam content within 24 hours.

The article says anyone who knows a game's mechanics can now build a similar one with a coding AI, even without development experience, a practice known as vibe coding, with results Koreans call ttalkkak games. Copiers no longer need the original code and can study the look and gameplay shown in a demo or trailer. OpenAI says its GPT-6 Astra, released in September, can create, host and share websites, web apps and games directly from a prompt. Clones were already a problem on user-generated content platforms such as Roblox and Fortnite, and the practice has now moved to the wider industry.

YNOT said it worried that a similar game made with AI could be accepted as the original simply because it came out first, and that the original could even be mistaken for plagiarism. Sini Ming wrote that closing the demo right away was only a temporary measure and not a fundamental solution, and that there is no way to stop it as individuals, but letting people know on social media might serve as a warning that Spookitchen is their game and that many people are watching over it. Sini Ming added a resolve to focus on development as usual. Alliance Arts cited concerns that a game imitating the demo's look and gameplay could reach the market before the original.

Some in the industry warn that if games built over years keep losing out to AI-made copies, the industry's foundations could start to crack. An indie developer with five years in the business likened recreating hit games with AI to a new kind of gold farming, saying someone could change only a game's appearance slightly with AI and release it over and over without doing any development. Kim Jeong-tae, a professor in the Department of Game Studies at Dongyang University, said developers increasingly want to hide their ideas rather than share them, and that the market is likely to turn into a battle of capital in which only big games AI cannot easily copy survive. Kim called for clear guidelines on what must not be done and a copyright safety net for indie and small and midsize game companies.

Articles.Title: Indie studios hide their demos as AI copycats circle

stories.Headline: Fears of AI being grafted onto North Korean hacking…“The gates of cyberattack hell have opened”
stories.Summary:
The FBI said on October 31 that North Korea was behind the theft of $6.3 billion from Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world. Binance said in its initial investigation that an engineer's laptop had been hacked and that weaknesses in the transaction approval system had been exploited. It also said there was no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked. The attackers targeted internal staff equipment before technical gaps in the system, a method North Korea has long used. No evidence has yet emerged that AI was used in the Binance attack.

Google Cloud and the security firm Wiz found that North Korean hacking groups have repeatedly posed as recruiters on social media to get employees at target companies to run malicious programs. A Microsoft Threat Intelligence report released on October 29 assessed that three out of eight North Korean hacking groups had reached a stage where AI is integrated into routine attack duties. Those three were said to use AI in live operations, beyond one-off trials. The domestic security firm Genians disclosed signs that the group Kimsuky had built an environment using a large language model and retrieval-augmented generation, which it viewed as an attempt to analyze stolen documents, extract information and automate attack duties. Since late September, more than 68,000 cases of personal information have been leaked at seven financial institutions including banks, and authorities estimated the same attacker used AI tools for large-scale, automated attacks.

Simon Choi, chief technology officer of the cybersecurity firm StealthMole, told the Financial Times that AI has given hackers wings. He said that because North Korea has a strong will to conduct cyberattacks, it is as if the gates of hell have opened. Microsoft said in its report that North Korea's AI-based operations are still under human involvement and are not at a fully autonomous stage. The domestic bank hacks targeted management blind spots such as loan broker systems, not core transaction networks. Blockchain investigation firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis attributed recent crypto heists to a North Korean group called TraderTraitor, which was named in a 2022 joint warning by the FBI, CISA and the US Treasury.

The Microsoft report said entities such as Andariel under the Reconnaissance General Bureau of North Korea have used the open-source AI penetration testing tool Artex in operations since late October. Traces of Artex were identified at the attack IP addresses in the bank cases. However, the timing differs from the bank attacks and the perpetrator has not been identified, so it is premature to link the two cases. The articles do not say what happens next.

Articles.Title: Fears of AI being grafted onto North Korean hacking…“The gates of cyberattack hell have opened”

stories.Headline: AI chat content carried over verbatim into filings… 80% of judges have “experienced fabricated precedents”
stories.Summary:
A judge recently came across a Supreme Court precedent cited in a brief that looked odd, and a check showed the case number had been made up by artificial intelligence. The Supreme Court's Court Administration Office announced on November 2 the results of a survey on citations of false AI precedents. The survey ran from the 6th to the 16th of the previous month among judges at courts of all levels and drew 360 responses. Eighty percent of the judges said they had seen false or non-existent precedents cited in civil, family and administrative cases.

Among the specific types, citation of a non-existent precedent was most common at 196 responses, or 80.7 percent. That was followed by citation of a false precedent at 159, or 65.4 percent, false or non-existent statutes at 41, or 16.9 percent, and false papers or other materials at 10, or 4.1 percent. Multiple answers were allowed. Judges described parties submitting fabricated judgments that copied the format of Supreme Court decisions, and in extreme cases language from chats with AI or from litigation strategy talks appeared in filings exactly as typed.

Asked who was responsible, 164 judges, or 69.5 percent, most often chose the party personally, while 136 judges, or 57.6 percent, also chose an attorney acting as litigation agent or defense counsel. The Supreme Court said citations of false or non-existent precedents from AI use burden the opposing party and the bench and delay the public right to a trial. Of the respondents, 91.7 percent said an institutional response is necessary, with 64.8 percent calling it very necessary. The most common proposed measure was a basis to impose fines, at 215 responses, or 61.4 percent.

Other proposed measures were a duty to verify cited precedents at 214, or 61.1 percent, a duty to disclose AI use at 212, or 60.6 percent, and sanctions such as referring attorneys for discipline at 194, or 55.4 percent. The Court Administration Office plans to pursue responses through amendments to the Civil Procedure Act and the Criminal Procedure Act. It will consult with relevant agencies, including the Ministry of Justice, to establish a legal basis for fines over false-precedent citations and will submit its views to the National Assembly. It also plans to consider measures such as guidance on AI precautions on the e-litigation website.

Articles.Title: AI chat content carried over verbatim into filings… 80% of judges have “experienced fabricated precedents”

stories.Headline: Shivamogga SP appeals to students to use social media, AI tools responsibly
stories.Summary:
Shivamogga Superintendent of Police B. Nikhil spoke to students on Tuesday at the 40th foundation day of Kuvempu University in Shankaraghatta. He appealed to them to use social media and artificial intelligence tools responsibly. He warned that careless use can harm students' careers and futures. He said unethical activities that start on social media are on the rise.

Mr. Nikhil said posts and comments that break the law, whether made while hiding one's identity or by mistake, can ruin a student's career. He said digital footprints cannot be erased once a person logs in and uses digital media. He said AI is spreading into every field, including education, and should be used to supplement studies rather than relied on entirely. He also urged students not to feel dejected if they do not land high-ranking posts, saying that doing any chosen job with sincerity is the real achievement.

Vice-Chancellor Sharath Ananthamurthy said students should not confine themselves to textbooks and should take an active part in art, literature and cultural activities. He said the university would provide more opportunities for distinctive learning experiences in the coming days. Registrar (Evaluation) Prof. R. Thimmarayappa, Dean of Student Welfare Prof. G. Prashanth Naik, deans Prof. S.K. Narasimhamurthy and Prof. Gajanana Prabhu, and extracurricular activities coordinator Dr. Talawar Venkatesh were present. Faculty members, non-teaching staff and students also attended.

Articles.Title: Shivamogga SP appeals to students to use social media, AI tools responsibly

stories.Headline: Ex-Kakao AI executive named head of public AI services task force
stories.Summary:
Kim Se-woong, a former Kakao executive who oversaw AI synergy initiatives, has been appointed to lead a government task force developing artificial intelligence services for the public. The Ministry of Science and ICT said on Monday that it had named Kakao's former vice president as head of the National AI Service Innovation Task Force. Kim founded and ran a tech startup, MightyWorks, in 2009 before joining Kakao, where he held senior roles in AI-related business and technology initiatives. The ministry said his experience in both AI services and organizational management would help the task force establish itself quickly and deliver services at a faster pace.

The task force, established this year, aims to develop and deliver AI services that address public needs by combining private-sector innovation with public-sector accountability. Unlike the traditional approach of outsourcing development to private contractors, the unit will directly identify public demand, address practical problems and build services in-house. It comprises four teams with a total of 61 members: 26 private-sector developers, 16 AI champions, 13 government officials and six experts from related organizations. The AI champions are practitioners trained and certified under a Ministry of the Interior and Safety program to lead the adoption of AI across government agencies.

Kim's term will run through September 2028. Kim said AI innovation that people can experience firsthand goes beyond introducing new technologies and starts with solving the inconveniences people face in their everyday lives. He said he would draw on his private-sector experience in AI technology and service development to combine the speed and innovation of private companies with public-sector accountability. He said he would deliver AI services that provide tangible benefits to the public as quickly as possible.

The ministry announced in August that it would recruit private-sector developers for the task force, before opening applications for the chief position in September. Kim was appointed following a selection process that included a review of applications and interviews. The task force will begin a new round of recruitment for private-sector developers in early November to strengthen its AI service development capabilities as it begins full-scale operations. Further details, including available positions, eligibility requirements and application timelines, will be announced on the ministry's website.

Articles.Title: Ex-Kakao AI executive named head of public AI services task force

stories.Headline: Incheon Int'l Airport uses AI to predict baggage system failures
stories.Summary:
Incheon International Airport Corp. began using an AI system at Terminal 2 on Oct. 26 to identify baggage-handling equipment at risk of failure. Sensors and machine-learning software monitor sorters, conveyor motors and arrival-hall carousels, flagging potential problems so crews can act before breakdowns. The airport expects preventive maintenance to reduce unexpected shutdowns and repair costs, extend equipment life and help prevent baggage delays. The BHS Smart Monitoring System displays results on a three-level scale: green for normal, yellow for caution and red for danger.

The system also identifies the likely cause of each flagged problem, allowing maintenance crews to replace parts or take other steps before a fault occurs. Previously, maintenance crews mostly repaired equipment after parts had failed. Cho Yong-soo, executive director of operations at Incheon International Airport Corp., said the system is expected to lower baggage-equipment management costs and improve passenger convenience. He added that the airport will continue to speed up the adoption of advanced digital technologies to make operations more stable and keep improving passenger convenience.

The BHS is a network of conveyors and sorting machines that moves checked luggage between check-in counters, aircraft and arrival halls. The system tracks key equipment in real time, including baggage sorters, the motors that drive the conveyors and the baggage carousels in arrival halls. Sensors collect data from the equipment, and machine-learning software analyzes it to find parts that are likely to fail. The airport said the switch to preventive maintenance is expected to prevent unexpected shutdowns, make equipment last longer and lower repair costs. It also expects fewer bags to be delayed, which would make travel easier for passengers.

Articles.Title: Incheon Int'l Airport uses AI to predict baggage system failures

stories.Headline: AI doomsday hype is "stealing all the attention" from immediate threats, Wharton's Mollick says
stories.Summary:
Wharton professor Ethan Mollick said in interviews with Axios and Business Insider, published on November 2, 2026, that the AI industry's focus on existential risk is pulling attention away from more immediate problems. He spoke around the release of his new book, "Co-Existence," which is described as a field guide to AI. He said that while people should worry about the apocalypse, there are about 1,000 other things he is really worried about that are already going to happen. He pointed to AI's effect on jobs as one example.

Mollick said the response should be policy that encourages AI to be used to augment work rather than automate it. He warned that if the panic about AI becomes only about it killing everyone, there will be no room to talk about anything else. He said the same technology that is damaging schools could also serve as a universal tutor, and that it might change health care for the better. He argued that people get to make choices about how the technology works and should focus on the upsides as well as the risks.

Mollick said most CEOs he talks to do not know what to do with the technology, and that pure automation is not what they want either. He said firing all your staff and replacing them with AI is not how you build competitive advantage, and that jobs tend to evolve, which can feel catastrophic or exciting depending on the job. He said he would like to see deep reporting on what is actually happening inside companies, and that worker and manager perspectives rarely come up. He said he uses AI for everything, and that while he writes his own drafts, AI found errors in his writing and in the sources he cited.

In the Business Insider interview, Mollick said advice to learn AI or find an AI-proof career, such as plumbing or nursing, is not very useful. He said that works until something like "PlumBot 6000" comes along, and that robotics experts he knows went from saying large language models were unrelated to robotics to saying there is something there. His book argues that the models are improving much faster than most people understand, and that the only way to deal with their rapid acceleration is to learn to live with them. That means accepting that much of what people can do today will be less useful in the future and focusing on the attributes they have that AI cannot replicate.

Articles.Title: AI doomsday hype is "stealing all the attention" from immediate threats, Wharton's Mollick says

stories.Headline: India's new AI-training framework is a repeat of old mistakes
stories.Summary:
India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology released a new framework last week aimed at breaking the data deadlock and widening access to data for building artificial intelligence models. The framework is called the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture for AI Training, and it is meant to allow responsible data sharing while ensuring privacy, transparency and trust. The article, published on 3 November 2026, was written by Rahul Matthan, a partner at Trilegal and the author of a book on India's approach to data governance. He argues that the framework is not a new architecture and that it undercuts much of what India's original DEPA was designed to achieve.

Under the original DEPA, decisions about what can be done with personal data sat with the data principal, but the new handbook moves that power to training data providers such as hospitals and banks. The handbook starts from the premise that individual consent is impractical at scale, and it makes those providers responsible for sourcing, curating and preparing datasets for AI training. It offers data principals little beyond a suggestion that providers could get priority access to the resulting models and a promise to explore royalties for them. Matthan writes that direct benefits will go only to model developers and the institutions that hold personal data, not to the people whose data was used.

Electronics and information technology minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says in his foreword that the framework is consent-based and user-controlled, which Matthan says the rest of the document contradicts. The principal scientific advisor calls it an elegant, India-specific solution in his foreword, but Matthan notes that secure data environments are not new. He points to Finland's 2019 law on secondary use of health and social data and the UK's 2022 Data Saves Lives strategy, which made secure data environments the default for National Health Service data. He also cites a 2022 project in which 71 institutions led by Penn Medicine trained a brain tumour model using federated learning in a confidential clean room.

Matthan traces part of the problem to an earlier mistake, when DEPA was called a consent management framework instead of a portability solution, and the term consent managers then entered the Digital Personal Data Protection Act with a different meaning. He describes the 40-page handbook as a word salad of technological jargon and regulatory buzzwords that promises more than it can deliver. He says the failings in it exceed anything he has seen before. The article does not say what the government or the ministry plans to do next.

Articles.Title: India's new AI-training framework is a repeat of old mistakes

stories.Headline: Copper Falls as Traders Assess AI Trade, US-Iran Diplomacy Hopes
stories.Summary:
Copper fell to a seven-week low on Tuesday as traders weighed the artificial-intelligence trade and the chances of diplomacy in the Middle East conflict. The metal dropped 2.2% on the London Metal Exchange to settle at $14,036 a metric ton, the lowest since Sept. 14. Comex copper fell 2.5% to settle at $6.4020 a pound. A drop in oil on unconfirmed reports of progress in peace talks in the US-Iran conflict pushed bond yields and the dollar higher, which weighed on metals priced in the US currency.

Concerns about the rollout of artificial-intelligence spending have hit equities in recent weeks, feeding fears about global growth and metals demand. South Korea's tech-heavy stock market came under pressure Tuesday, while a rebound in a gauge of chipmakers sent US equities higher. RBC Capital Markets analysts wrote that the selloff has put the AI demand narrative behind copper's rally under renewed scrutiny. Copper is still up about 13% this year, but Tuesday's decline threatens to push prices out of a range held over the past two months.

The 2026 rally was largely driven by expectations that the US would impose import tariffs on refined metals, and uncertainty over Washington's plans is now weighing on prices. Metals broadly can benefit from demand tied to spending on AI-linked infrastructure, but copper has stood out as a potential major winner. Tin, used in soldering electric circuitry, also fell 4.5% to the lowest since April. All other base metals on the LME declined.

Articles.Title: Copper Falls as Traders Assess AI Trade, US-Iran Diplomacy Hopes

stories.Headline: Day 2 - Microsoft AI Boom, Election Eve, & FOMC Wait
stories.Summary:
A user on the moomoo community site posted a discussion on November 2, 2026, under the name AnnaG. The post recapped Microsoft's quarterly results, which the user said included record revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19 percent from a year earlier. The user also cited diluted earnings per share of $4.92 on a GAAP basis. According to the post, Microsoft recently changed how it reports revenue to show its shifting focus.

Under that new breakdown, the post said, $76.8 billion came from AI agents and infrastructure, while devices and consumer brought in $15.5 billion. The user said they hold Microsoft stock with an average cost of $410 and are sitting on an unrealized profit. They said strong cloud and AI growth gave them confidence to keep the position through current macro uncertainty. The post also noted the midterm elections were one day away.

The user wrote that stocks have historically rallied once election uncertainty clears and said they did not feel a need to reduce risk. They called corporate demand for AI infrastructure a long-term trend that should outweigh short-term political volatility. They also flagged the Fed's rate decision as the last major macro event that week. In their view, Microsoft's cash generation and position in AI make it a defensive tech play, and they said its balance sheet could handle a hawkish surprise from the Fed.

The post carried a disclaimer saying the community is offered by Moomoo Technologies Inc. for educational purposes only. It showed about 20,000 views and one comment at the time. The article did not say what the Fed decided or how the elections turned out. It also gave no further details on what happens next.

Articles.Title: Day 2 - Microsoft AI Boom, Election Eve, & FOMC Wait

stories.Headline: AI debt is hitting record levels at the worst possible time
stories.Summary:
Wall Street is facing a growing challenge to the AI investment boom, which has delivered most of the S&P 500's gains since the bull market began four years ago. The flood of AI investment has shifted this year from cash generated by the biggest tech companies to borrowing. Tech sector debt issuance has reached around $623 billion this year, according to Wells Fargo data, a record share of borrowing from nonbank companies. Wells Fargo analysts estimate that around a third of this year's AI capital spending has been financed in the bond market.

The four largest hyperscalers, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta Platforms, need $730 billion in capital spending this year, with another $1 trillion-plus expected in 2027. Adding lower-credit-quality borrowing from companies such as Oracle and neocloud spending from the likes of CoreWeave takes the 2027 tally to around $1.6 trillion. The cost of that debt is rising: the investment-grade spread has risen to around 95 basis points from around 74 a year earlier, and spreads on AI related high-yield debt are nearing 350 basis points, the most since May 2025. Oracle raised $10 billion in debt this week plus $10 billion in stock, Microsoft closed a $25 billion bond deal last week, Alphabet sold a $6.7 billion euro-denominated deal and Meta is reportedly preparing another $20 billion in debt after a $97 billion equity raising last month.

Lawrence Gillium of LPL Financial says the divergence in spreads reflects a rational assessment that is likely to continue. He says the investment-grade gap should narrow if the buildout slows and supply eases, while the high-yield gap reflects real exposure to the buildout itself. He adds that losses would show up first at the leveraged end of AI credit if spending slows. S&P Global revised the outlook on Meta's AA credit rating to negative last week, citing a dramatic increase in leverage and a free cash flow outlook likely to remain negative beyond 2028.

Investors' main question has shifted from who is gaining the most ground in the AI buildout to who is ready to generate the best return on capital already committed. S&P 500 profits are expected to rise around 36% this year, with 2027 growth expected at less than half that pace. The Federal Reserve is expected to raise its benchmark rate for a second time this year in December, and next year's deficit is expected to pass $2 trillion. Henry Allen of Deutsche Bank says wider spreads raise the cost of capital and tighten financial conditions, making investment harder to justify.

Articles.Title: AI debt is hitting record levels at the worst possible time

stories.Headline: Cohere Hits US$25bn as Canada & NVIDIA Fund Sovereign AI
stories.Summary:
Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E funding round targeting up to CAD7bn, or US$5bn, at a valuation of CAD35.7bn, or US$25.5bn, according to a November 2, 2026 article in AI Magazine. The round is the largest private financing round ever undertaken by a Canadian technology company. Backers include the Schwarz Group as lead investor, returning investor NVIDIA, Bell Ventures, Bullhound Capital, Inovia Capital, Prosperity7 Ventures and the Government of Canada. Bloomberg had reported the week before that Cohere was raising a large round at a US$20.5bn pre-money valuation.

Canada has committed to an equity investment of up to about CAD1.6bn, or US$1.1bn, to be made in stages. As part of the deal the government says the investment will create at least 1,000 new high-paying Canadian technical jobs by 2030, and Cohere will commit at least CAD1.7bn, or US$1.2bn, to additional computing infrastructure in Canada by 2030. Cohere will keep its Canadian incorporation and headquarters, invest in Canadian research partnerships, create opportunities for students and recent graduates, and keep working with the Canadian AI Safety Institute. Cohere says the money will accelerate frontier enterprise models, full-stack AI products, solutions for regulated industries and long-term compute infrastructure. The company says its customer base grew 20 times over the past year to 300 customers, including Aston Martin Aramco, Bell Canada, Fujitsu, RBC, RWS, PwC, TD Bank and TKMS.

Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez said the company was founded in Canada on the belief that the country could build AI companies able to compete at the highest level globally, and that the investment helps attract world-class talent and build secure, sovereign technology from Canada for customers around the world. He said organisations need greater control over their data, infrastructure and how AI is deployed. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada's investment is an investment in choice and security, and that true sovereignty depends on the ability to build, adopt and govern AI on the country's own terms. He said it is in all Canadians' interests for Cohere to succeed and that Canadians will now have a share in that success.

The article frames the round as part of a broader global shift toward sovereign AI, with the US and China currently dominating through firms such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Moonshot, and challengers emerging in Europe, including Mistral. Cohere has expanded across the UK and Europe, including a combination with Germany's Aleph Alpha and the planned acquisition of Czech cybersecurity company AISLE. The founders said they will use the funds to build what they called a frontier company outside the US and China. The article does not say what happens next beyond the initial close of the round.

Articles.Title: Cohere Hits US$25bn as Canada & NVIDIA Fund Sovereign AI

stories.Headline: AI Security | Automated AI Security Testing
stories.Summary:
CrowdStrike announced on November 3, 2026, that it plans to acquire Dreadnode, a company whose work supports automated AI security testing. The announcement came from CrowdStrike and was tied to its Fal.Con Europe event, where the company presented its latest innovations. The deal is meant to advance AI trust and to deliver automated AI security testing for what CrowdStrike calls the agentic enterprise. CrowdStrike also published a press release and a blog post about the acquisition alongside the announcement. The articles describe the problem the acquisition targets rather than the deal's price or closing terms.

They say AI models and agents are probabilistic, meaning they can be jailbroken, manipulated through prompt injection, and can fail in ways conventional software testing was never built to catch. Those weaknesses sit inside the model and the agent's reasoning loop, a layer traditional security testing never reaches, and most enterprises have no way to find them before deployment. Conventional testing, such as pentests, probes code rather than cognition, so it misses prompt injection and model-specific flaws. CrowdStrike frames the acquisition as a way to test every AI model, application, and agent for security weaknesses before deployment. The stated goal is to find AI weaknesses before attackers do, using real techniques to find what breaks and what to fix before deployment.

The company presents the deal as advancing AI trust for the agentic enterprise. No individual executive is named or quoted in the articles, so responsibility is attributed to CrowdStrike as a company. The context is CrowdStrike's broader push into AI security, which includes AI detection and response, agent security, and services such as frontier AI readiness and resilience. The articles do not give the acquisition price, a closing date, or other deal terms. They also do not say what happens next beyond the stated plan to acquire Dreadnode and deliver automated AI security testing.

Articles.Title: AI Security | Automated AI Security Testing

stories.Headline: Microsoft Q1 FY 2027: Copilot Consumption Expands the AI Business
stories.Summary:
Microsoft reported its Q1 FY 2027 results on November 2, 2026, with revenue of $92.28 billion, up 19% year over year and above the Wall Street consensus of $90.63 billion. Agents and Infra revenue was $76.80 billion, up 25%, while Devices and Consumer revenue was $15.48 billion, down 3%. Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9 billion, up 30%, and Azure revenue rose 48%. Operating income was $45.92 billion, up 21%, at a margin of about 50%, and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $4.89, up 18%.

Copilot now combines subscription and consumption billing, and daily users rose nearly 50% quarter over quarter and more than fivefold year over year. Customers actively consuming credits through usage-based billing grew more than 75% quarter over quarter, and GitHub agents open more than one-third of pull requests. Foundry passed 120,000 customers, with revenue more than tripling year over year, and Microsoft added 24 data centers across five continents. Fabric exceeded 44,000 paid customers, and the Agent 365 registry passed 50 million agents.

Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and chief executive officer, said the company announced its biggest Copilot update to date, bringing Chat, Cowork, Autopilot and Code into one unified experience. He said it is one product experience across commercial and consumer with all of Office built in, and described Copilot as the new operating system for work. The analyst take said Microsoft's challenge is turning deeper usage into durable customer value while keeping infrastructure availability and sales practices aligned with demand. It also noted weaker sales execution in Microsoft 365 E3 and standalone offerings and an expectation of slower consumption adoption outside coding.

Microsoft guided Q2 FY 2027 revenue to $96 billion to $97.1 billion, or 18% to 19% growth, with Agents and Infra at $80.1 billion to $80.7 billion. It expects Azure growth of 49% to 50% at constant currency and a Microsoft Cloud gross margin of about 65%. Capital expenditures are expected to exceed $50 billion in Q2, and calendar-year 2026 spending of about $170 billion reflects delayed third-party capacity deliveries. The article says the next phase depends on converting expanding AI usage into recurring consumption revenue while improving returns on infrastructure investments.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Q1 FY 2027: Copilot Consumption Expands the AI Business

stories.Headline: Why Anthropic's AI warning is targeting investors | The Global Story
stories.Summary:
Anthropic has issued a warning about artificial intelligence that is aimed at investors, according to a BBC Global Story segment dated 3 November 2026. The warning was covered in a BBC programme that examines why the company is directing its message at people who put money into AI. The same date appears on the BBC listing for the episode. The articles do not give further details of what the warning says.

The articles give no numbers, dates or names beyond the 3 November 2026 date and the company name Anthropic. They do not describe any requirement or change that the warning brings. They also do not say what specific action, if any, investors are being asked to take. No further specifics are provided in the source material.

The articles do not name anyone responsible for the warning or give any statements from Anthropic or its officials. No paraphrased comments from the company appear in the material. The only attribution is to the BBC programme The Global Story. The articles do not say who else, if anyone, was involved.

The context given is limited to the BBC listing, which places the segment among other news items from the same date. The articles do not say what happens next after the warning. They do not describe any response from investors or regulators. No follow-up steps are mentioned in the source material.

Articles.Title: Why Anthropic's AI warning is targeting investors | The Global Story

stories.Headline: ChatGTP and the Search for Truth: OpenAI Says It Receives 70 Million Religion Requests Weekly
stories.Summary:
OpenAI has said that ChatGPT receives about 70 million religion-related questions every week, according to an analysis reported by The Christian Post and covered by the Billy Graham Evangelistic Association on November 2, 2026. The analysis found that Islam-related questions make up nearly half of all religious questions, while Christianity-related questions make up about one-third. About 22 million of the 70 million questions centered on studying religious texts, and about 16 million pertained to religious holidays and practices. Hinduism was the third most researched religion at 4%, followed by Judaism at 2% and Buddhism at 1%.

The report said religion topics spiked around certain holidays, with Christianity-related questions rising around Easter and Islam-related questions rising around Ramadan and Eid al-Adha. For Christianity-related questions, almost 50% pertained to Bible passages, and about 13% related to worship, sermons or church practices. The researchers said AI is becoming a tool for religious people to support their religious lives and deepen their understanding of their faith. They also said faith leaders are using AI to support their work teaching and organizing those they serve.

The OpenAI researchers said AI should help people pursue what matters to them, including their faith, while strengthening rather than replacing human relationships and institutions. They said AI is not and should not become an arbiter of religious truth or a replacement for spiritual guidance, roles they said belong to individuals, religious leaders and congregations. John Stonestreet, president of the Colson Center for Christian Worldview, told Decision earlier this year that the source of truth is Scripture alone, not artificial intelligence. Clayton Chancey, an enterprise AI architect and founder of Foray Consulting, said the great call is to discernment and warned against offloading or outsourcing discernment to a machine.

Articles.Title: ChatGTP and the Search for Truth: OpenAI Says It Receives 70 Million Religion Requests Weekly

stories.Headline: Anthropic Builds World's Tiniest Dam Against AI Clone Game Flood
stories.Summary:
Anthropic recently added new rules to the guidelines that govern Claude, its AI assistant, according to a report by Game Developer cited by Aftermath. A Claude user noticed the update in the last few days, and Anthropic confirmed the change. The new rules say Claude should build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. They also say Claude should not build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original.

Anthropic employee Addy Osmani said in a tweet that the sentences were added to steer Claude away from recreating someone else's specific game, because using Claude to infringe intellectual property is against the company's usage policy. He said original games, genre games, and games built from users' own designs and assets are meant to keep working. Eurogamer reported that some users ran into problems with the new rules during what they felt was legitimate use. One said they make personalized digital modules of board wargames under paid commission for clients, from games the clients own, and another had trouble making a single-player version of a board game for internal study. A user on the Claude subreddit said Claude refused to tweak a single-player version of Carcassonne it had made for them.

Aftermath reported that the change is unlikely to do much to stop AI clones of games, because people can use other tools if Claude refuses, and because the programs are easy to trick with workarounds. The article said users do not have to ask directly for a specific game, and gave the example of asking for a game about an Italian plumber with a mustache who travels through pipes. It also said the discourse on the Claude subreddit was divided, with some people saying it is good that Anthropic will stop people from stealing, others noting the whole thing is built on theft, and still others seeing it as the games industry clamping down because companies got afraid they would lose revenue. The article said it is unlikely there will be any meaningful change.

Articles.Title: Anthropic Builds World's Tiniest Dam Against AI Clone Game Flood

stories.Headline: Fujifilm to boost tape production 5x as AI fuels archiving demand
stories.Summary:
Fujifilm announced on Thursday that it will invest roughly 10 billion yen, about $63 million, to increase its production capacity for magnetic tape fivefold. The company said the spread of generative AI is producing exponential growth in data needs worldwide, which is driving demand for archiving. The 5x increase will be measured against fiscal year 2025 production levels. The investment covers the Kanagawa Factory, Odawara site, and Fujifilm called it the largest investment it has made to date in dedicated LTO tape facilities.

The project will run from fiscal years 2026 through 2028 to fund manufacturing expansion and additional personnel. The extra capacity is primarily meant to produce the latest-generation FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium10 tape. Fujifilm's history with magnetic tape as a data storage medium dates back to the 1950s, and in 2000 the company released its first LTO Ultrium storage tape. In 2011 it was the first to commercially produce tape with barium ferrite magnetic particles, and in 2025 it debuted the LTO Ultrium10, the first storage solution in the medium to use what the company calls fine hybrid magnetic particles by combining barium ferrite with strontium ferrite tech.

Fujifilm said major cloud service and data center operators have been expanding their use of magnetic tape because it can store large data volumes at relatively low cost. Tape backups can be easily disconnected and stored in a drawer, a vault, or a separate facility. The company highlights the ability to air-gap tape cartridges as a last defense for user data. Given the sophistication of cyberattacks, Fujifilm said, magnetic tape is attracting increasing attention as a means of protecting data from threats such as ransomware.

Articles.Title: Fujifilm to boost tape production 5x as AI fuels archiving demand

stories.Headline: Meta Rolls Out AI Business Assistant To All Advertisers, Agencies 04/24/2026
stories.Summary:
Meta has begun rolling out the beta version of its AI business assistant to advertisers and agencies of all sizes across major global markets and languages, according to an announcement from the company this week. The tool first launched with small businesses in the U.S. last October. Meta says businesses using the automated assistant resolved common account issues at a 20% higher rate. They also saw a 12% decrease in ad cost per result after applying the assistant's opportunity score recommendations.

The assistant is designed to improve campaign performance through tailored AI-powered recommendations and real-time guidance based on an account's business data. It can also quickly restore disabled accounts, update spend limits, and troubleshoot payment or delivery errors. Advertisers and agency partners can reach it within Ads Manager, Meta Business Suite, and Business Support Home. Meta said it will keep iterating the assistant based on advertiser feedback, and that expanded capabilities focused on campaign planning and creation are expected throughout 2026.

Meta described the assistant as part of its broader AI push, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg saying on the company's Q4 investor call that AI is starting to understand users' personal context, including their history, interests, content and relationships. He said much of what makes agents valuable is the unique context they can see. The expansion comes as Meta cuts its employee base while investing heavily in AI chips, top AI talent, data centers and AI acquisitions, including the purchase of the AI agent and social-media platform Moltbook. Meta's earlier chatbots on Instagram drew criticism after being flagged for flirting and romantic role play with underage users and for generating racist and violent remarks, and after The Washington Post reported that the chatbots gave teen accounts information about how to commit suicide. Meta then said teens would no longer be able to access AI characters until an updated experience is ready.

Articles.Title: Meta Rolls Out AI Business Assistant To All Advertisers, Agencies 04/24/2026

stories.Headline: AT&T and Amdocs Expand Collaboration, Bringing Together Amdocs aOS and AT&T's AI-Enabled Framework to Simplify Operations and Improve Customer Experiences
stories.Summary:
AT&T and Amdocs announced on November 3, 2026 that they are expanding their longstanding collaboration through an eight-year agreement to modernize AT&T's business and customer operations using AI. The deal pairs Amdocs aOS, the company's agentic operating system for telecommunications, with AT&T's AI-enabled delivery framework. The companies said they will work as one delivery team, combining AT&T's technology environment and business priorities with Amdocs' telecom and engineering expertise. The goal is to simplify operations, improve efficiency, deliver new products and services faster, and enhance customer experiences.

Under the agreement, the two companies will share responsibility for delivering projects faster while reducing the total cost of modernizing and operating critical systems. Amdocs, which is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol DOX, reported revenue of $4.53 billion in fiscal 2025. AT&T says it serves more than 100 million U.S. families, friends and neighbors, plus nearly 2.5 million businesses. Amdocs has more than 40 years of experience serving communications companies.

Jeremy Legg, Chief Technology Officer at AT&T, said the company is changing how it builds and operates technology so it can move faster and deliver more for customers. He said AI delivers the greatest value when it is grounded in the business, technology and people it supports, and that bringing together shared expertise can simplify complex work and bring new products and experiences to customers faster. Shimie Hortig, President and Chief Executive Officer of Amdocs, said the real test of AI in telecom is whether it can transform mission-critical systems and fundamentally change how communications companies operate. She said AT&T's approach to AI and its ambition to rethink technology delivery reflect its leadership in the industry.

The companies described the agreement as building on decades of trust between them. Amdocs said its aOS brings industry-specific AI into core business processes, advancing customers toward intelligent, increasingly autonomous operations across business, IT and network domains. Amdocs also included a forward-looking statement noting risks and uncertainties that could cause future results to differ from expectations, including macroeconomic conditions, trade policies and tariffs, competition, security incidents and the potential loss of a major customer. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the terms of the agreement.

Articles.Title: AT&T and Amdocs Expand Collaboration, Bringing Together Amdocs aOS and AT&T's AI-Enabled Framework to Simplify Operations and Improve Customer Experiences

stories.Headline: The rules of getting ahead are changing in the AI era. Not everyone stands to benefit
stories.Summary:
Microsoft chief economic opportunity officer Aneesh Raman has been predicting the death of the traditional career ladder as AI reshapes the workplace. He spoke at Aspen Digital's WIN Summit in late October, where Fortune's Kristin Stoller asked him about the implications for women and other historically marginalized groups. Raman envisions a "climbing wall" in place of the ladder, where progress isn't always upward and workers chart their own paths based on their skills, interests and opportunities. He acknowledged that losing the familiar career playbook could initially be intimidating.

Raman argued the change could ultimately give workers more freedom to advance in ways that suit their strengths and ambitions. He said that over time people start to climb in ways unique to them. Part of the answer, he said, is "radical transparency," meaning workers should understand how AI is changing their jobs and what opportunities they have to shape their own careers. He also believes women could have an edge in the AI era because they over-index on human skills such as empathy and judgement. He predicts more women will become CEOs and that women's representation on corporate boards could climb from roughly a third to half or more.

New research from Nicole Smith, a senior researcher at Pew Research Center, found that in more AI-exposed occupations, men's employment grew 6.3% for each one-point increase in an occupation's exposure score, while women's barely changed. Among workers with a high school diploma or less, women's employment fell. Smith said men are much more optimistic about AI than women and may be more inclined to use it to pursue new opportunities. She said the conversation needs to change and be opened to women. The question now, according to the article, is whether employers can make career advancement more flexible without making the path to success less equitable.

Articles.Title: The rules of getting ahead are changing in the AI era. Not everyone stands to benefit

stories.Headline: Vodafone Business UK Selects Amdocs to Drive Agentic Transformation of B2B Operations with aOS
stories.Summary:
Amdocs announced on November 3, 2026, that Vodafone Business UK, the enterprise arm of VodafoneThree, has selected it to lead the agentic transformation of its B2B operations. The program will consolidate and upgrade multiple legacy business support systems onto a unified agentic platform built on Amdocs' BSS capabilities and powered by Amdocs aOS, its agentic operating system specialized for telecommunications. Amdocs will act as Lead Systems Integrator and long-term technology partner, overseeing implementation and supporting the platform's ongoing operation and evolution. The companies say the work is meant to create simpler customer journeys, accelerate the launch of new products and services, and lay the foundation for an agentic operating model.

For Vodafone Business customers, the transformation is designed to make services easier to buy, manage and support, while giving Vodafone greater flexibility to respond to changing business needs and introduce new offerings. Amdocs aOS will bring agentic capabilities across implementation and ongoing operations, supporting a move toward more intelligent, automated workflows that can continuously evolve. Amdocs is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the ticker DOX and reported revenue of $4.53 billion in fiscal 2025. VodafoneThree is investing £11 billion in its network and services over 10 years.

Jon Ryan, Business Enablement Director at VodafoneThree, said the ambition is to give every business customer a simpler, faster and more consistent experience, backed by the UK's best network and the right digital foundations. He said the companies are consolidating B2B systems and transforming how Vodafone operates, introducing agentic capabilities that can automate workflows, continuously evolve and respond to changing customer needs. Anthony Goonetilleke, Group President, Growth Horizons at Amdocs, said communications service providers are moving beyond experimentation with AI and focusing on embedding agentic intelligence into the core of their operations at scale. He said the combination of aOS, proven BSS capabilities and deep telecom expertise is meant to help Vodafone Business build a more agile, intelligent operating model that can accelerate time to market, simplify the end-to-end customer journey and respond faster to changing business needs.

Amdocs describes itself as having more than 40 years of experience serving the world's leading communications companies, combining proprietary technology, deep industry expertise and end-to-end accountability from transformation through ongoing operations and evolution. The company says it runs billions of transactions daily and brings industry-specific AI into core business processes, advancing customers toward intelligent, increasingly autonomous operations across business, IT and network domains. VodafoneThree is a UK communications business serving consumers, businesses and public-sector organisations with mobile, broadband and digital services, and Vodafone Business helps organisations connect people, places and things through connectivity, cloud, cybersecurity and Internet of Things solutions. The press release did not say when the transformation is scheduled to be completed.

Articles.Title: Vodafone Business UK Selects Amdocs to Drive Agentic Transformation of B2B Operations with aOS
